For a mode with pure isotope-dependent reduced mass
(H
\to
D:
m_{D}=2m_{H}
, same force constant since the
electronic potential is isotope-invariant):

\omega^{D}/\omega^{H}=1/\sqrt{2}
, so

\Delta E_{\mathrm{ZPE}}=\tfrac{1}{2}\hbar\omega^{H}(1-1/\sqrt{2})
per mode.
For the three C–H/D bending modes in S
{}_{\mathrm{N}}2

with
\omega_{H}^{\mathrm{react}}\approx 1350
cm
-1

(tetrahedral) and
\omega_{H}^{\mathrm{TS}}\approx 1000
cm
-1
(trigonal-bipyramidal,

[
223
]
):

\displaystyle\Delta E_{\mathrm{ZPE}}^{\mathrm{react}}

\displaystyle\approx(1-1/\sqrt{2})\times 3\times\tfrac{1}{2}\hbar\omega_{H}^{\mathrm{react}}\approx 7.1\;\text{kJ/mol},

\displaystyle\Delta E_{\mathrm{ZPE}}^{\mathrm{TS}}

\displaystyle\approx(1-1/\sqrt{2})\times 3\times\tfrac{1}{2}\hbar\omega_{H}^{\mathrm{TS}}\approx 5.3\;\text{kJ/mol},

\displaystyle\Delta^{2}E_{\mathrm{ZPE}}

\displaystyle\approx 1.8\;\text{kJ/mol}.

Hence
k_{H}/k_{D}\approx\exp(1800/(8.314\times 298))\approx 2.1
at 298 K.
The experimental value
k_{H}/k_{D}\approx 1.3
for

\alpha
-trideuteromethyl S
{}_{\mathrm{N}}2

[
174
]
is smaller than this
classical ZPE-dominated estimate because (i) not all
three bending modes shift by the full
1350\to 1000\;\mathrm{cm}^{-1}
(partial symmetry breaking at
TS); (ii) weak coupling to other modes violates strict
Streitwieser cutoff, reducing the ratio;
(iii) the
u^{H}/u^{D}
prefactor correction in
(
21
) is non-negligible at these
frequencies.
The exact value follows from evaluating
(
20
) with the full set of ab initio
normal-mode frequencies at both geometries — a purely

\mathcal{L}_{5}
calculation.

Tower language.

Equations (
21
) and
(
22
) are
\mathcal{L}_{5}
theorems:
they require

(a)

g
to obtain the mass ratio
m_{D}/m_{H}=2

(Remark
8.2
: the metric
distinguishes H from D, invisible at

\mathcal{L}_{4.5}
);

(b)

\nabla^{2}_{g}V|_{\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{min}}}
for
reactant frequencies;

(c)

\nabla^{2}_{g}V|_{\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{TS}}}
for
TS frequencies;

(d)

the full TST coherence condition
(
19
) with
\kappa_{H}=\kappa_{D}
.

Items (b) and (c) are Hessians of
V_{\mathrm{full}}
,
computable from
F_{\!V}
and
g
at specific critical
points — pure
\mathcal{L}_{5}
data.
At
\mathcal{L}_{4.5}
neither the geometry
\mathbf{R}^{*}
nor
the curvature
\nabla^{2}_{g}V
exists; the secondary KIE
is therefore invisible at
\mathcal{L}_{4.5}
and confirms

\mathrm{coker}(\varphi_{5})\neq 1
.
∎

Remark 8.41

(Tower attribution of tunneling: the

\mathcal{L}_{5}
/
\mathcal{L}_{7}
boundary is sharper than textbook
pedagogy suggests)
.

Proposition
8.40
establishes the secondary
KIE as an
\mathcal{L}_{5}
theorem.
For
primary
KIEs — including the anomalously
large values observed in enzymatic hydrogen-transfer
reactions — the tower attribution requires care:
textbook treatments identify “quantum tunneling”
with “nuclear wavefunctions on the BO surface” and
conclude
\mathcal{L}_{7}
is needed.
This identification is incorrect.
The
\mathcal{L}_{5}
/
\mathcal{L}_{7}
boundary is drawn by the

dimensionality of the nuclear wavefunction

required, not by the mere presence of quantum effects:

The tower criterion.

\mathcal{L}_{5}
admits quantum information at fixed geometry
or along low-dimensional reaction paths: harmonic
ZPEs (Hessian spectra at critical points), 1-D
anharmonic proton vibrational states in PES slices
(vibrationally adiabatic potential cuts), semiclassical
tunneling actions along instantons or corner-cutting
paths, and ring-polymer imaginary-time quantum
statistics.

\mathcal{L}_{7}
is reserved for the
multidimensional
nuclear wavefunction on the full nuclear
configuration space
: states on the full nuclear
Hilbert space
\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{nuc}}
, not
restrictions to 1-D slices or frozen environments.

Semiclassical tunneling is
\mathcal{L}_{5}
.

All standard tunneling corrections — Wigner, Bell,
Eckart, small-curvature tunneling (SCT), large-curvature
tunneling (LCT), microcanonical optimised
multidimensional tunneling (
\mu
OMT)

[
286
,
29
]
— require only the PES,
Hessians along the MEP, and (for LCT) off-MEP PES data
for corner-cutting paths.
No nuclear wavefunction is constructed.
Ring-polymer instanton theory (RPI)

[
250
]
computes the dominant
tunneling trajectory as an imaginary-time classical
orbit on the inverted PES — a stationary-phase saddle
of the path integral — requiring only the PES.
Perturbative corrections to RPI

[
192
]
achieve few-percent
agreement with exact nuclear QM on benchmark systems
using only PES and its derivatives.

Enzymatic KIEs of 20–700 are
\mathcal{L}_{5}
.

Soybean lipoxygenase wild type shows
k_{H}/k_{D}\approx 80
at 25
∘
C
[
171
]
;
the L546A/L754A double mutant reaches
k_{H}/k_{D}\approx 540
–
700

[
150
]
, several
orders of magnitude above the 298 K semiclassical ZPE
ceiling of
\sim 7
–
9
.
These values are quantitatively reproduced by
vibronically nonadiabatic proton-coupled electron
transfer (PCET) models

[
193
,
131
]

and by ensemble-averaged variational TST with
\mu
OMT
tunneling corrections (EA-VTST/
\mu
OMT,

[
9
]
).
Both frameworks construct the rate from 1-D proton
vibrational wavefunctions in frozen active-site
geometries plus semiclassical WKB actions along
reaction-path tunneling routes.

No multidimensional nuclear wavefunction is
constructed.

By the tower criterion above these calculations are

\mathcal{L}_{5}
: they use
(F_{\!V},g)
plus low-dimensional
quantum refinements that remain “shadowed” by the
PES.

What forces
\mathcal{L}_{7}
.

Genuine
\mathcal{L}_{7}
phenomena are those requiring the

multidimensional nuclear wavefunction on the
full nuclear configuration space
as a primary
object.
These include:

•

MCTDH wavepacket propagation for reactive
scattering (full nuclear Schrödinger equation on
the BO surface);

•

Colbert–Miller DVR for full quantum reaction
rates on small systems;

•

exact nuclear diagonalisation for tunneling
splittings in highly symmetric systems, below the
instanton-validity crossover temperature where
perturbative RPI fails to converge;

•

ortho/para nuclear-spin statistics, which
requires the full nuclear wavefunction to enforce
Bose/Fermi symmetry under the
G^{*}
-action of

\mathcal{L}_{4.5}
(the symmetry group exists at

\mathcal{L}_{4.5}
; its consequences for the total
nuclear-spin-symmetrised wavefunction live at

\mathcal{L}_{7}
);

•

the superselection-sector structure of
molecular identity (see Chapter
10
).

In the tower,
\mathcal{L}_{7}
is forced by phenomena that

cannot
be reduced to
\mathcal{L}_{5}
data plus
semiclassical corrections — not merely by the
presence of large KIE values or strong quantum
behaviour.
The forcing argument for
\mathcal{L}_{5}\Rightarrow\mathcal{L}_{7}

(§
8.7
) is grounded in such
phenomena.

8.5.3. Cross-level consistency:
F_{\!H}

and
F_{\!V}

The TST coherence condition links
F_{P}
(
\mathcal{L}_{3}
) to

F_{\!V}
(
\mathcal{L}_{5}
) via (
19
).
An analogous cross-level consistency links
F_{\!H}

(
\mathcal{L}_{1}
) to
F_{\!V}
(
\mathcal{L}_{5}
): the standard enthalpy of
a reaction, computed thermochemically from tabulated
formation enthalpies at
\mathcal{L}_{1}
, agrees with the
electronic-energy drop computed from the BO PES at

\mathcal{L}_{5}
, up to well-understood corrections.
Two logically distinct statements must be kept separate.

•

Hess’s law

[
139
]
: the
enthalpy functor
F_{\!H}:\mathcal{L}_{1}(P)\to(\mathbb{R},+)

respects reaction composition,

F_{\!H}(r_{2}\circ r_{1})=F_{\!H}(r_{2})+F_{\!H}(r_{1})
.
This is
\mathcal{L}_{1}
-functoriality, established in
Chapter
3
from the state-function
character of enthalpy (
H=U+pV
); it is
automatically independent of
\mathcal{L}_{5}
data (BO,
RRHO, geometry) because it lives four levels
below.

•

BO/RRHO decomposition of
F_{\!H}
:
a representation theorem expressing the single
real number
F_{\!H}(r)
in terms of
\mathcal{L}_{5}
data —
the PES, its Hessians, and thermal partition
functions.
This presupposes the BO approximation and the
rigid-rotor harmonic-oscillator (RRHO)
factorisation of the molecular partition function.

Proposition
8.43
below
establishes the BO/RRHO decomposition and identifies
it as the cross-level consistency between
\mathcal{L}_{1}
and

\mathcal{L}_{5}
.

Observation 8.42

(BO/RRHO decomposition of
F_{\!H}
)
.

The standard molar reaction enthalpy is expressible
in terms of
\mathcal{L}_{5}
data as

F_{\!H}(r)\;=\;\underbrace{\Delta V_{\mathrm{elec}}(r)}_{F_{\!V}\text{ at
minima}}+\;\underbrace{\Delta E_{\mathrm{ZPE}}(r)}_{\nabla^{2}_{g}V\text{ at minima}}+\;\underbrace{\Delta E_{\mathrm{therm}}(T,r)}_{\text{partition functions}}+\;\underbrace{RT\,\Delta n_{\mathrm{gas}}(r)}_{pV\text{ correction}},

(23)

where:

•

\Delta V_{\mathrm{elec}}(r)=V_{\mathrm{full}}^{(r)}(\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{prod}})-V_{\mathrm{full}}^{(r)}(\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{react}})

is the PES electronic-energy difference between
product and reactant minima (extracted from

F_{\!V}(r)
);

•

\Delta E_{\mathrm{ZPE}}(r)=\tfrac{1}{2}\hbar[\sum_{i}\omega_{i}^{\mathrm{prod}}-\sum_{j}\omega_{j}^{\mathrm{react}}]
is the harmonic
zero-point-energy difference (eigenfrequencies
of
\nabla^{2}_{g}V
at the minima);

•

\Delta E_{\mathrm{therm}}(T,r)
collects
thermal contributions from the RRHO partition
functions (translational, rotational, and
vibrational populations above
ZPE)
[
232
,
136
]
;

•

RT\,\Delta n_{\mathrm{gas}}(r)
is the
pV

correction converting
\Delta U
to
\Delta H

for gas-phase reactions (
\Delta n_{\mathrm{gas}}

= change in moles of gas; zero for
condensed-phase reactions).

For most condensed-phase reactions at 298 K
(
\Delta n_{\mathrm{gas}}=0
, rotational and
translational thermal contributions nearly cancel
between products and reactants for similar-sized
molecules):
F_{\!H}(r)\approx\Delta V_{\mathrm{elec}}(r)+\Delta E_{\mathrm{ZPE}}(r)
, with residual error

\lesssim 5\;\mathrm{kJ/mol}
.

Equation (
23
) is the BO/RRHO decomposition
of
F_{\!H}

[
232
,
136
]
.
It is a representation theorem for a single
F_{\!H}(r)
,

not
a composition law; the composition law is
Hess’s law, established independently at
\mathcal{L}_{1}
.

Proposition 8.43

(Cross-level consistency of
F_{\!H}

and
F_{\!V}
)
.

Let
U_{5\to 1}:\mathcal{L}_{5}(P)\to\mathcal{L}_{1}(P)
denote the
composite forgetful functor

U_{5\to 4.5}\circ U_{4.5\to 4}\circ U_{4\to 3}\circ U_{3\to 2}\circ U_{2\to 1}
dropping
F_{\!V}
,

G^{*}
-equivariance, DPO structure,
F_{P}
, and
F_{\!S}

in sequence.
Let
\widetilde{F_{\!H}}_{F_{\!V}}:\mathcal{L}_{5}(P)\to(\mathbb{R},+)

denote the
\mathcal{L}_{5}
-derived enthalpy functor
assigning to each reaction the right-hand side of
(
23
).
Then there exists a natural transformation

\eta:\;F_{\!H}\circ U_{5\to 1}\;\Longrightarrow\;\widetilde{F_{\!H}}_{F_{\!V}},

between functors
\mathcal{L}_{5}(P)\to(\mathbb{R},+)
.
The component
\eta_{r}=0
for all
r
in the
harmonic + ideal-gas + BO limit
(i.e.,
\eta
is the zero natural transformation),
and
|\eta_{r}|\lesssim 5\;\mathrm{kJ/mol}
at 298 K
for rigid molecules with no low-frequency torsions.
The following diagram commutes up to
\eta
:

Proof.

Step 1: BO decomposition of the enthalpy.

By the BO prescription (Definition
8.14
),

V_{\mathrm{full}}(\mathbf{R})=E_{0}(\mathbf{R})
is the
electronic ground-state energy.
The molecular internal energy at temperature
T

factorises in the RRHO approximation as

U(T)\;=\;E_{0}(\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{min}})+E_{\mathrm{ZPE}}+E_{\mathrm{therm}}(T),

where
E_{\mathrm{ZPE}}=\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{i}\hbar\omega_{i}

and
E_{\mathrm{therm}}(T)
collects populations above
ZPE plus rotational and translational kinetic-energy
contributions
[
232
,
136
]
.
The standard enthalpy is
H^{\circ}=U^{\circ}+pV=U^{\circ}+n_{\mathrm{gas}}RT
(ideal-gas limit).
For a reaction
r
:

F_{\!H}(r)\;=\;\Delta H^{\circ}(r)\;=\;\Delta V_{\mathrm{elec}}(r)+\Delta E_{\mathrm{ZPE}}(r)+\Delta E_{\mathrm{therm}}(T,r)+RT\,\Delta n_{\mathrm{gas}}(r),

which is (
23
).

Step 2: Functoriality at
\mathcal{L}_{5}
.

The right-hand side of (
23
) defines

\widetilde{F_{\!H}}_{F_{\!V}}
as a monoidal functor

\mathcal{L}_{5}(P)\to(\mathbb{R},+)
: for a composite reaction

r_{2}\circ r_{1}
, each of the four terms is a
difference of object-level quantities and adds across
composition (the telescoping of minima energies;
likewise for ZPE, thermal, and
pV
terms).

\widetilde{F_{\!H}}_{F_{\!V}}
therefore respects reaction
composition — it is a functor into
(\mathbb{R},+)

structurally analogous to Hess’s law but defined on

\mathcal{L}_{5}
.

Step 3:
\eta=0
in the harmonic + ideal-gas
+ BO limit.

Step 1 shows
F_{\!H}(r)=\widetilde{F_{\!H}}_{F_{\!V}}(r)
in
this limit.
Pulling
F_{\!H}
back along
U_{5\to 1}
gives two
coincident functors
\mathcal{L}_{5}(P)\to(\mathbb{R},+)
, so

\eta_{r}=0
for all
r
.

Step 4: Anharmonic and non-ideal corrections.

Beyond the harmonic + ideal-gas + BO limit,
\eta_{r}

captures:
(i) anharmonic corrections to ZPE (VPT2, VCI;
typically 1–5% of ZPE for hydrides);
(ii) real-gas corrections to
pV
;
(iii) higher-order BO corrections
(
\sim(m_{e}/M)^{1/4}
; negligible at chemical accuracy);
(iv) quasi-harmonic corrections for low-frequency
torsions and floppy modes.
For condensed-phase reactions at 298 K involving rigid
molecules with no low-frequency torsions, the total
residual
|\eta_{r}|\lesssim 5\;\mathrm{kJ/mol}
, well
within the accuracy of standard electronic-structure
methods.

Step 5: Tower interpretation.

The coincidence
F_{\!H}\circ U_{5\to 1}\approx\widetilde{F_{\!H}}_{F_{\!V}}
means the
values

F_{\!H}(r)
are constrained by
\mathcal{L}_{5}
data: each
individual reaction enthalpy is expressible via

(F_{\!V},g)
plus RRHO partition functions.
This does
not
reduce Hess’s law to BO/RRHO:
Hess’s law is the independently established

\mathcal{L}_{1}
-functoriality of
F_{\!H}
(composition law),
which survives any replacement of the right-hand side
of (
23
) by a non-BO treatment.
What BO/RRHO establishes is that
F_{\!H}(r)
, for each
individual
r
, admits a representation in terms of

\mathcal{L}_{5}
data — a statement about pointwise values,
not about composition.
∎

Remark 8.44

(Hess’s law and BO/RRHO are logically
independent)
.

The distinction made in Step 5 of the proof deserves
emphasis: Hess’s law and the BO/RRHO decomposition are
statements of different kinds at different tower
levels.

•

Hess’s law
=
\mathcal{L}_{1}
-functoriality of

F_{\!H}
on reaction networks.
Content: composition law

F_{\!H}(r_{2}\circ r_{1})=F_{\!H}(r_{2})+F_{\!H}(r_{1})
,
established at
\mathcal{L}_{1}
from the state-function
character of enthalpy
[
139
]
, and
therefore automatically independent of
\mathcal{L}_{5}

data (BO, RRHO, geometry).
It survives in systems where BO fails
— conical intersections, non-adiabatic dynamics,
ultrafast photochemistry — because its
derivation does not use BO.

•

BO/RRHO decomposition
= object-level
(pointwise) representation of
F_{\!H}(r)
via

\mathcal{L}_{5}
data.
Content: for each reaction
r
, the real number

F_{\!H}(r)
decomposes as
(
23
).
This is a cross-level consistency statement
(
\mathcal{L}_{1}\!\leftrightarrow\!\mathcal{L}_{5}
) about pointwise
values, presupposing BO and the RRHO
factorisation of the molecular partition function.

In a categorical presentation the two can be
conflated (both involve “the enthalpy functor”),
but they are distinct statements and must be cited
distinctly: Hess
[
139
]
and the
state-function treatment of enthalpy for the former;
Ochterski
[
232
]
and the RRHO
thermochemistry treatment of
Helgaker–Jørgensen–Olsen for the latter.

Remark 8.45

(The tower is coherent: higher levels
constrain lower ones pointwise)
.

Proposition
8.43
exemplifies
a general pattern: the
pointwise values
of every
lower-level functor in the tower admit a
BO/RRHO-type representation in terms of
\mathcal{L}_{5}
data

(F_{\!V},g)
in the appropriate approximation.

•

F_{\!H}(r)\approx\Delta V_{\mathrm{elec}}(r)+\Delta E_{\mathrm{ZPE}}(r)

(from
F_{\!V}
at minima and Hessians; this section).

•

F_{\!S}(r)
: partition-function ratio at

\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{min}}
, requiring the full
Hessian spectrum — an
\mathcal{L}_{5}
datum.

•

F_{P}(r)=\kappa(k_{B}T/h)(Q^{\ddagger}/Q_{\mathrm{reac}})e^{-V^{\ddagger}/k_{B}T}
: full TST
from
F_{\!V}
, Hessians at
\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{TS}}

and
\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{min}}
, plus semiclassical
corrections for
\kappa
— all
\mathcal{L}_{5}
data.

The composite forgetful functor
U_{5\to k}

(for
k=1,2,3
) therefore corresponds to a

projection
from the
\mathcal{L}_{5}
geometric level
onto its thermochemical (
k=1
), equilibrium
(
k=2
), or kinetic (
k=3
) shadow at the level of
pointwise values.

Crucially, this pointwise coherence does not reduce
the
composition laws
(Hess’s law, detailed
balance, the chemical master equation) to
\mathcal{L}_{5}
:
these are functoriality statements established at
their own levels from level-specific physics, and they
survive replacements of the
\mathcal{L}_{5}
representation of
individual values.
The tower is a coherent filtration
pointwise
,
not a tower in which each level is derived from the
next one up.

Continuing Example

.

At
\mathcal{L}_{5}

and its dimension; (ii) the PES landscape with its

8.6.1.
\mathrm{S_{N}2}
:
configuration orbifold, PES, and TST coherence

Example 8.46

(
\mathrm{S_{N}2}
at
\mathcal{L}_{5}
)
.

The running example is

\mathrm{CH_{3}Cl\;+\;OH^{-}\;\longrightarrow\;CH_{3}OH\;+\;Cl^{-}},\quad T=298\;\mathrm{K}.

Configuration orbifold.

The reactive system contains
n=7
atoms
(C, Cl, O, and 5 H atoms counted together).
By Observation
8.4
:

\dim\bigl({C_{e}}(G)\bigr)\;=\;3n-6\;=\;3(7)-6\;=\;15\quad\text{internal coordinates.}

At the transition state, the relevant internal
coordinates include the
r(\mathrm{C{\cdots}Cl})
and

r(\mathrm{C{\cdots}O})
distances (the two bond-changing
coordinates), the H–C–H angles, and the H–C–Cl and
H–C–O angles.
The transition-state geometry has
C_{3v}
symmetry
(Proposition
8.6
applied below),
reducing the effective dimensionality of the search to
the symmetric subspace.
The accessible region
{C_{e}}^{\mathrm{acc}}(G)
has two
connected components (one per enantiomeric face of the

\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}

from
\mathcal{L}_{4.5}

(Proposition

).

The BO PES
V:{C_{e}}(G)\to\mathbb{R}
for this system
has the characteristic double-well profile of a

\mathrm{S_{N}2}

•

Reactant ion-dipole complex

[\mathrm{CH_{3}Cl{\cdots}OH^{-}}]

of the lax monoidal structure

and

8.4.1

•

Transition state
at
\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{TS}}

the symmetric pentacoordinate structure with

r(\mathrm{C{\cdots}Cl})=r(\mathrm{C{\cdots}O})\approx 2.4
Å. In the gas phase, the intrinsic
barrier from the ion-dipole complex is modest
(
\sim 40
–
60
kJ/mol at MP2/6-31G*); aqueous
solvation raises the activation Gibbs free energy
substantially. The relevant quantity for comparison
with the experimental aqueous rate constant is the
solvent-corrected activation Gibbs free energy

from separated reactants in standard state
,

\Delta G^{\ddagger}\approx 97
kJ/mol (MP2/6-31G*
with implicit-solvent correction, 298 K, 1 M standard

•

Product ion-dipole complex

[\mathrm{CH_{3}OH{\cdots}Cl^{-}}]
: a symmetric
exit-channel well.

•

Product asymptote
: separated

\mathrm{CH_{3}OH}
and
\mathrm{Cl}^{-}
,
lying
\approx 75
kJ/mol below the reactant
asymptote (exothermic, consistent with

F_{\!H}(r)=-75
kJ/mol at
\mathcal{L}_{1}

Intrinsic reaction coordinate.

The IRC runs in the mass-weighted metric
g

(Definition
8.1
) from

uphill through

\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{TS}}

The reaction coordinate is dominated by the

the unique negative-curvature mode of
V
at

\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{TS}}

[

,

]
.
The three H–C–H angles change monotonically from

\approx 109.5^{\circ}
) in the reactant complex
through planar (

to the C–Cl/C–O axis) at the TS
to inverted tetrahedral (
\approx 109.5^{\circ}
) in the
product complex. This is the

the geometric trajectory along which the chirality
descriptor
\sigma
changes sign. The combinatorial

encoded at

).

TST coherence check.

The
\mathcal{L}_{3}
datum is the experimental bimolecular

F_{P}(r)=k_{r}\approx 6\times 10^{-5}
M
-1
s
-1

at 298 K in water
[

]
.
The

datum is the activation Gibbs free energy

\Delta G^{\ddagger}\approx 97
kJ/mol from the solvated

For a
bimolecular
reaction, the TST coherence
condition (Definition
8.38
)
takes the form:

k_{r}^{\mathrm{TST}}\;=\;\frac{k_{B}T}{h}\,\exp\!\left(\frac{-\Delta G^{\ddagger}}{RT}\right)\quad\text{[M${}^{-1}$s${}^{-1}$]},

where
\Delta G^{\ddagger}=E_{a}-T\Delta S^{\ddagger}

is the Gibbs free energy of activation and the

s
-1
is understood with an implicit standard

M to give the

[
288
]
.

Prediction from the activation Gibbs
energy.

Using
\Delta G^{\ddagger}=97
kJ/mol in the
TST coherence expression:

k_{r}^{\mathrm{TST}}\;=\;\frac{k_{B}T}{h}\,e^{-97000/(8.314\times 298)}\;=\;(6.21\times 10^{12})\times e^{-39.1}\;\approx\;6\times 10^{-5}\;\mathrm{M^{-1}s^{-1}}.

Comparison with experiment.

The experimental rate inverted through TST gives

\Delta G^{\ddagger}_{\mathrm{expt}}\;=\;-RT\ln\!\left(\frac{k_{r}}{k_{B}T/h}\right)\;=\;-(2.479)\ln\!\left(\frac{6\times 10^{-5}}{6.21\times 10^{12}}\right)\;\approx\;97\;\mathrm{kJ/mol},

matching the computed barrier within the harmonic and
standard-state approximations.
The TST coherence condition holds to within the
precision of the calculation: the computed

\Delta G^{\ddagger}
from the solvated PES and the
experimentally derived
\Delta G^{\ddagger}
from the
measured rate constant agree. Residual discrepancies
at the level of
\sim 1
–
2
kJ/mol arise from the
harmonic approximation to the TS partition function,
the standard-state convention, and the level of
electronic-structure theory; all are themselves

\mathcal{L}_{5}
-computable refinements.

The
\mathcal{L}_{3}
rate constant is in this sense

constrained
by
\mathcal{L}_{5}
geometric data: not
determined exactly — TST is an approximation — but
tightly bracketed by the activation Gibbs free energy
on the solvated PES.

Point group at the TS.

The TS geometry
\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{TS}}
has a
three-fold axis through Cl–C–O and three mirror
planes, each containing the axis and one H atom.
By Proposition
8.6
:

P_{\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{TS}}}\;\cong\;C_{3v},

realised in
O(3)
as the spatial image of the
subgroup of
\mathrm{Aut}_{\mu}(G)\times\langle E^{*}\rangle

that stabilises
\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{TS}}
in
{C_{e}}(G)
.
This is the
\mathcal{L}_{5}

\mathcal{L}_{4.5}
: the

G^{*}

\mathrm{S_{N}2}
DPO rule
manifests geometrically as the

point group
of the TS.

Berry connection.

The
\mathrm{S_{N}2}
IRC lies entirely on the
ground-state BO surface with no degeneracy of the

on a simply-connected open neighbourhood
U
of the reaction path.
By Proposition

:

A_{0}\big|_{U}\;=\;0,\quad w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}|_{U})\;=\;0,\quad c_{1}(L_{0}|_{U})\;=\;0.

The orbital analysis confirms this: the LUMO of

This is the

8.6.2.
\mathrm{N_{2}O_{4}}\rightleftharpoons 2\,\mathrm{NO_{2}}
:
two minima, a transition state, and cross-level coherence

Example 8.47

(
\mathrm{N_{2}O_{4}}
dissociation at
\mathcal{L}_{5}
)
.

Continuing Example
4.33
(
\mathcal{L}_{2}
).
This system provides a particularly clean illustration
of cross-level coherence (§
8.5
) because
the PES has a single internal coordinate of primary
importance, the thermochemical data are accurately
known
[
204
]
, and the kinetics are
experimentally well-characterised.

Configuration orbifold.

\mathrm{N_{2}O_{4}}
has
n=6
atoms; the products

2\,\mathrm{NO_{2}}
have
n_{1}=n_{2}=3
atoms each,
but the combined reactive system has
n=6
atoms
throughout (the N–N bond dissociates but no atoms are
created or destroyed).
The combined
{C_{e}}(G)
has dimension
3(6)-6=12

internal coordinates; the dominant reaction coordinate
is the N–N bond length
r_{NN}
, so a one-dimensional
PES profile along
r_{NN}
captures the essential physics.

PES schematic.

•

Reactant minimum
at
r_{NN}\approx 1.78
Å: the
D_{2h}
-symmetric
\mathrm{N_{2}O_{4}}

equilibrium structure.
Take
V(\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{min,react}})=0
as
the energy reference.

•

Variational transition state
: the
N–N bond dissociation has
no
index-1 saddle
on the BO PES in the strict Morse sense.
V
rises
monotonically along
r_{NN}
with negligible reverse
barrier for radical recombination. The relevant
“transition state” is a variational dividing
surface, located by minimising the unimolecular rate
expression rather than by finding a stationary point
of
V

[
288
]
. The
effective barrier lies in the range

E_{a}\approx 50\text{--}57
kJ/mol; the lower bound
corresponds to the inner-wall barrier, while the
upper bound approaches the dissociation energy

\Delta H^{\circ}=+57.0
kJ/mol (see below). This
places the example formally outside the
Morse-saddle morphism class of
\mathbf{Orb}^{\mathrm{Morse}}

(Definition
8.24
); the variational
setting belongs to the generalised

\mathcal{L}_{5}
-with-free-energy-surfaces extension, which
treats the dividing surface as a chosen morphism
datum rather than a critical point of
V
.

•

Product asymptote
at
r_{NN}\to\infty

two separated
C_{2v}
-symmetric
\mathrm{NO_{2}}

V(\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{prod}})=F_{\!H}(r_{1})=+57.0
kJ/mol
[

]
,
consistent with
\mathcal{L}_{1}
(endothermic dissociation).

The PES profile is monotonically increasing along

r_{NN}
with a broad, loose maximum — the
archetypal profile of a bond-dissociation reaction
with little reverse barrier.

Intrinsic reaction coordinate.

The IRC is approximately the N–N stretching coordinate

r_{NN}
, with small contributions from the N–O
stretching and O–N–O bending modes.
As
r_{NN}
increases from 1.78 Å to
\infty

P_{\mathbf{R}}\cong D_{2h}
at the reactant
minimum, decreasing to
C_{2v}\times C_{2v}
(two
non-interacting
\mathrm{NO_{2}}
fragments) as

. By
Proposition
8.6
, both point

of the corresponding stabiliser subgroup of

\mathrm{Aut}_{\mu}(G)\times\langle E^{*}\rangle
at the
respective geometries.

TST coherence check.

The
\mathcal{L}_{3}
datum is

k_{1}=4.8\times 10^{4}
s
-1
at 298 K
(first-order dissociation rate constant).
The TST coherence condition with

kJ/mol (lower bound) gives:

k_{1}^{\mathrm{TST}}\;=\;\frac{k_{B}T}{h}\,e^{-50000/(8.314\times 298)}\;=\;(6.21\times 10^{12})\times e^{-20.17}\;\approx\;1.1\times 10^{4}\;\mathrm{s}^{-1}.

This is within a factor of
\sim
5 of the

\mathcal{L}_{3}
datum (
4.8\times 10^{4}
s
-1
): the TST
coherence condition holds at order-of-magnitude

The remaining factor of
\sim
5 is accounted for by
the
activation entropy

\Delta S^{\ddagger}>0
,
which is expected and large for a loose bond-dissociation

k_{1}\;=\;\frac{k_{B}T}{h}\,e^{\Delta S^{\ddagger}/R}\,e^{-E_{a}/RT}.

For
\Delta S^{\ddagger}\approx+30
J mol
-1
K
-1

(typical for a loose TS):

e^{\Delta S^{\ddagger}/R}=e^{30/8.314}\approx 37
,
giving an upper bound
k_{1}\approx 37\times 1.1\times 10^{4}\approx 4\times 10^{5}
s
-1
. The

4.8\times 10^{4}
s
-1
lies
between the entropy-free lower bound

1.1\times 10^{4}
s
-1
and the

\Delta S^{\ddagger}
-corrected upper bound

4\times 10^{5}
s
-1
: TST coherence holds within
the precision available from a one-dimensional PES

Pinning

V

at

Cross-level coherence:

For

Tower language.

The

for

.

,

: the

\mathrm{N_{2}O_{4}}\to 2\mathrm{NO_{2}}
path stays on

\mathrm{NO_{2}}

.

Both coherences fail to be exact at

for

§8.7. What
\mathcal{L}_{5}
cannot express:
forcing of
\mathcal{L}_{6}

The entire
\mathcal{L}_{5}
framework rests on Layer 2(b) of
§
8.3
: the ground-state section

\sigma_{0}
is a smooth section of
{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}
on the
relevant CI-free open subset of
{C_{e}}(G)
, equivalently,
no conical intersection (CI) between
V_{0}
and
V_{1}

lies in the chemically accessible region traversed
by the IRC and its low-energy basins. Within this
restriction
\mathcal{L}_{5}
completely describes ground-state
thermal chemistry via the Morse triple

({C_{e}}(G),V_{0},g)
.
But Layer 2(b) is not permanent.
It fails for a large class of chemically important
processes, and the failure is not a matter of
approximation quality: it is a
topological
obstruction invisible to
V_{0}
.

The key point is that
\mathcal{L}_{5}
records only the
ground-state PES function
V_{0}
, not the electronic
bundle that fibres over it.
A CI is a
geometric
feature of
{C_{e}}(G)
where

V_{0}(\mathbf{R})=V_{1}(\mathbf{R})
.
At the CI itself the eigenvalue
V_{0}
is continuous
but not smooth (Wigner–von Neumann normal form: a
conical singularity with
V_{0}\sim V_{\mathrm{CI}}-|\mathbf{x}|
in the two-dimensional branching plane).
On the complement
{C_{e}}(G)\setminus X_{\mathrm{CI}}

where the eigenvalues are isolated,
V_{0}
is smooth
and the
\mathcal{L}_{5}
datum cannot detect that the CI exists
nearby: only the topology of the complement, encoded in the
ground-state line bundle
L_{0}
(or equivalently, in its
real sub-bundle
L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}
under time-reversal
symmetry), distinguishes systems with and without the CI.

What changes is the topology of the bundles over the
punctured base
{C_{e}}(G)\setminus X_{\mathrm{CI}}
.
Both
L_{0}
(the complex ground-state line bundle) and
its real sub-bundle
L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}
generated by the
real-gauge section
\tilde{\sigma}_{0}

(Proposition
8.21
) are well-defined
on this complement, and both carry topological
invariants:

c_{1}(L_{0})\in H^{2}({C_{e}}(G)\setminus X_{\mathrm{CI}},\mathbb{Z}),\qquad w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})\in H^{1}({C_{e}}(G)\setminus X_{\mathrm{CI}},\mathbb{Z}/2).

Which of these is the informative invariant is set by
the codimension of
X_{\mathrm{CI}}
in
{C_{e}}(G)
:

•

For a
real-symmetric

\hat{H}_{\mathrm{el}}

(spinless non-relativistic electrons with
time-reversal-invariant Coulomb interactions),
degeneracies of the
2\times 2
effective block
require two real conditions to vanish (trace shift
and off-diagonal coupling), so
X_{\mathrm{CI}}
has

codimension 2
. A small loop
S^{1}
encircling

X_{\mathrm{CI}}
is a 1-cycle, and the natural
invariant of the bundle around it lives in

H^{1}(\cdot,\mathbb{Z}/2)
. This is
w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})
, and
it is non-trivial: a sign holonomy of
-1
around the
loop witnesses the Longuet–Higgins
effect
[
205
,
216
,
41
]
. The Chern class
c_{1}(L_{0})
around the
same loop is automatically zero — not because

L_{0}
is globally trivial, but because the loop
bounds no canonical 2-chain in the punctured
complement, so the
H^{2}
-pairing does not detect
codimension-2 obstructions.

•

For a
complex Hermitian

\hat{H}_{\mathrm{el}}

without time-reversal symmetry (e.g. in an external
magnetic field or with spin-orbit coupling),
degeneracies require three real conditions and

X_{\mathrm{CI}}
has
codimension 3
. A small
sphere
S^{2}
around an isolated CI point is a
2-cycle, and
c_{1}(L_{0})
measured by

\int_{S^{2}}\Omega_{0}/2\pi\in\mathbb{Z}
becomes the
Berry-monopole charge.

For the thermal molecular chemistry of

\mathcal{L}_{6}
— real-symmetric Hamiltonian, codimension-2 CI
seams — the relevant invariant is therefore

w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})
, and the molecular Aharonov–Bohm
phenomenon is the
\mathbb{Z}_{2}
sign holonomy.
c_{1}
remains
a well-defined invariant of
L_{0}
in its own right; it
just measures a different (codimension-3) obstruction
that is not generically present without breaking
time-reversal symmetry.

\mathcal{L}_{5}
sees
\sigma_{0}
only as a function (the PES);

\mathcal{L}_{6}
sees it as a section of a bundle with
non-trivial
\mathbb{Z}_{2}
-holonomy. The step from function
to bundle section — and from numerical to topological
invariant — is the deepest geometric step in the
tower.

Concrete illustration:
H + H
2
.

The hydrogen-exchange reaction has a smooth
ground-state PES with a collinear TS barrier of

\approx 9.6
kJ/mol and a TST rate in good agreement
with experiment — at
\mathcal{L}_{5}
the reaction appears
fully understood.
Yet a CI exists at the equilateral
D_{3h}
geometry,
off the collinear IRC but within the configuration
space explored by the nuclear wavefunction at reactive
collision energies.
Any loop encircling the
D_{3h}
CI acquires a
Longuet–Higgins sign holonomy of

-1

[
205
]
, producing a predicted
interference alternation in the reactive differential
cross-section of H + HD
[
158
]
.
The single-surface
\mathcal{L}_{5}
calculation cannot recover
this signature, because
w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})=0
is imposed
by construction via Layer 2(b) (which restricts to the
simply-connected CI-free open subset of
{C_{e}}(G)
), not computed.

Forcing pair for
\mathcal{L}_{6}
:
identical ground-state PES, distinct Hilbert bundle
topology

Idealised setup.

Consider two systems
(V_{0}^{A},L_{0}^{A})
and

(V_{0}^{B},L_{0}^{B})
on the same configuration orbifold

{C_{e}}(G)
, where
V_{0}^{\bullet}
is the ground-state
PES and
L_{0}^{\bullet}\to{C_{e}}(G)
the associated
ground-state line bundle:

(i)

PES identity
:
V_{0}^{A}(\mathbf{R})=V_{0}^{B}(\mathbf{R})
for all
\mathbf{R}\in{C_{e}}(G)

— pointwise identical ground-state energy, same
IRC, same activation barrier, same TST rate.

(ii)

Distinct bundle topology
: system A
has
w_{1}(L_{0}^{A,\mathbb{R}})=0
(Layer 2(b) holds on a
simply-connected open subset of
{C_{e}}(G)
covering
the chemically accessible region; Berry connection
can be gauged to zero), whereas system B has a CI
seam
X_{\mathrm{CI}}^{B}\subset{C_{e}}(G)
of
codimension 2 (two real conditions on the

2\times 2
effective electronic Hamiltonian:
trace-shift and discriminant both vanish) on which

V_{0}^{B}(\mathbf{R})=V_{1}^{B}(\mathbf{R})
. The
complement
{C_{e}}(G)\setminus X_{\mathrm{CI}}^{B}

acquires non-trivial
\pi_{1}
from loops encircling
components of
X_{\mathrm{CI}}^{B}
, and around such
loops
w_{1}(L_{0}^{B,\mathbb{R}})\neq 0
in
H^{1}({C_{e}}(G)\setminus X_{\mathrm{CI}}^{B},\mathbb{Z}/2)
.

At the CI itself
V_{0}^{B}
has the cone singularity
described above; away from
X_{\mathrm{CI}}^{B}
it is
smooth and (by hypothesis) pointwise equal to
V_{0}^{A}
.
The classical IRC need not visit
X_{\mathrm{CI}}^{B}

at all; what matters is that loops in
{C_{e}}(G)\setminus X_{\mathrm{CI}}^{B}
encircling
X_{\mathrm{CI}}^{B}
are
non-contractible, and nuclear wavefunctions supported
near the IRC can be probed along such loops.

This idealised pair is hypothetical — two real
molecular systems with pointwise-identical
V_{0}
but
different CI topology are not generically realised in
nature. The forcing argument is a categorical

test of expressive power
: it asks whether the

\mathcal{L}_{5}
datum
({C_{e}}(G),V_{0},g)
contains enough
information to distinguish system A from system B,
and the answer is
no
. In actual chemistry, the
A vs B distinction manifests as the difference between
reactions whose accessible nuclear region encloses a
CI (e.g. H + HD reactive scattering at high collision
energies) and those whose region does not (e.g. ground-state
\mathrm{S_{N}2}
at thermal conditions).

Chemical instances.

•

Type A
(CI-free in the accessible
region): thermal chemistry on the globally smooth
real sub-bundle
L_{0}^{A,\mathbb{R}}
; sign holonomy
trivial;
w_{1}(L_{0}^{A,\mathbb{R}})=0
. Fully captured at

\mathcal{L}_{5}
. Prototype:
\mathrm{S_{N}2}
,
§
8.46
.

•

Type B
(accessible region encircles

X_{\mathrm{CI}}
): the nuclear wavefunction is
supported on a region of
{C_{e}}(G)\setminus X_{\mathrm{CI}}^{B}
that contains non-contractible
loops around components of
X_{\mathrm{CI}}^{B}
. Any
such loop acquires sign holonomy
-1
, the molecular
Aharonov–Bohm effect
[
216
,
41
]
. Because the total (electronic
\times

nuclear) wavefunction must be single-valued on

{C_{e}}(G)\setminus X_{\mathrm{CI}}^{B}
, the sign
change of the electronic eigenstate around such a
loop forces a compensating sign change of the
nuclear wavefunction — equivalently, the nuclear
wavefunction is double-valued on the base and
single-valued on a double cover
[
205
]
. This produces observable
interference in product channels. Prototype:
H + HD
[
158
]
; the canonical
chemical realisation is developed in
§
9.1
.

Indistinguishability at

\mathcal{L}_{5}
.

The Morse triple
({C_{e}}(G),V_{0},g)
coincides for A
and B by condition (i), so
F_{\!V}
assigns the same
object of
\mathbf{Orb}^{\mathrm{Morse}}
to both.
The Stiefel–Whitney class
w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})
is not a
datum of
\mathcal{L}_{5}
: it is not computable from

({C_{e}}(G),V_{0},g)
, and at
\mathcal{L}_{5}
, Layer 2(b)
restricts to a simply-connected CI-free open subset
where
w_{1}
vanishes by construction. The swap

\phi_{6}=[A\leftrightarrow B]
is therefore a
non-trivial element of
\mathrm{coker}(\varphi_{6})
in the
automorphism (pointed-set) exact sequence

1\;\to\;\ker\varphi_{6}\;\to\;\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{L}_{6}(P))\;\xrightarrow{\;\varphi_{6}\;}\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{L}_{5}(P))\;\to\;\mathrm{coker}(\varphi_{6})\;\to\;1,

(24)

following the tower’s standard pointed-set
convention:
\mathrm{coker}(\varphi_{6}):=\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{L}_{5}(P))/\mathrm{im}(\varphi_{6})
as a pointed quotient, a group
when
\mathrm{im}(\varphi_{6})
is normal in the
codomain and a coset space otherwise; the forcing
content is the same in either case. The map

\varphi_{6}
is the restriction on automorphisms induced
by the forgetful functor
U_{6\to 5}:\mathcal{L}_{6}(P)\to\mathcal{L}_{5}(P)
.

The construction of
\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{L}_{6}(P))
is deferred to
Chapter
9
; at this stage (
24
)
is a design constraint stating that any categorical
structure
\mathcal{L}_{6}
receiving the CI topology datum must
have non-trivial cokernel over
\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{L}_{5})
.
Non-trivial
\mathrm{coker}(\varphi_{6})
proves that
\mathcal{L}_{6}
is
strictly richer than
\mathcal{L}_{5}
: the
\mathbb{Z}_{2}
sign
holonomy
w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})
(and the associated CI seam

X_{\mathrm{CI}}\subset{C_{e}}(G)
) is irreducibly new
structure.

The extension
\mathcal{L}_{5}\to\mathcal{L}_{6}
differs in character
from every previous extension in the tower.
All lower extensions add structure
on
the
configuration orbifold — a PES function, a metric,
a Morse structure, DPO rules,
G^{*}
-equivariance.
The
\mathcal{L}_{5}\to\mathcal{L}_{6}
extension adds structure

over

{C_{e}}(G)
: the topology of the Hilbert
bundle
{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}\to{C_{e}}(G)
whose fibres carry the electronic wavefunctions.

The new data that
\mathcal{L}_{6}
introduces — the CI seam

X_{\mathrm{CI}}\subset{C_{e}}(G)
(codimension 2 for
real-symmetric
\hat{H}_{\mathrm{el}}
, codimension 3
when time-reversal symmetry is broken), the Berry
connection
A_{0}
on
L_{0}
together with its real-gauge
sign holonomy on
L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}
, and the two
codimension-matched invariants

w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})\in H^{1}({C_{e}}(G)\setminus X_{\mathrm{CI}},\mathbb{Z}/2),\qquad c_{1}(L_{0})\in H^{2}({C_{e}}(G)\setminus X_{\mathrm{CI}},\mathbb{Z}),

— are developed in
§§
9.2
–
9.4
. For thermal
molecular chemistry in the real-symmetric regime, the
informative invariant is
w_{1}
and the forcing pair
above demonstrates its non-triviality; for systems with
broken time-reversal symmetry (external magnetic
fields, spin-orbit coupling),
c_{1}
becomes informative
and the codimension-3 Berry-monopole regime applies.

\mathcal{L}_{6}
accommodates both regimes; the molecular
Aharonov–Bohm forcing pair lives in the
w_{1}
regime.

§9.
\mathcal{L}_{6}
: The Electronic Structure Level

§9.1. Forcing the extension: half-integer
pseudorotation quanta in
\mathrm{Na_{3}}

The vibrational spectrum of
\mathrm{Na_{3}}
in its

2^{2}E^{\prime}
excited electronic state, measured by
Delacrétaz, Grant, Whetten, Wöste, and
Zwanziger
[
75
]
,
is the canonical molecular example of fractional
pseudorotational quantisation. In the ideal
free-pseudorotor model, an ordinary single-valued
scalar nuclear wavefunction on the pseudorotation
circle has integer angular quantum numbers
j=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,\ldots
. The Jahn–Teller Berry sign
changes the boundary condition to
\psi(\phi+2\pi)=-\psi(\phi)
, so the allowed quantum numbers
become
j=\pm 1/2,\pm 3/2,\pm 5/2,\ldots
.
The lowest pseudorotational level lies at

\hbar^{2}/(8I_{\mathrm{ps}})
above the trough minimum
in this limit, with no
j=0
level in the
topological sector.
1
1

1

The
\mathrm{Na_{3}}

B
-system assignment has a subsequent rovibronic
and pseudo-Jahn–Teller literature
[
213
,
217
]
.
The half-integer pseudorotational description used here is the canonical Berry-phase interpretation of the observed fractional quantisation; raw line positions alone do not uniquely determine an effective Hamiltonian, and quantitative corrections from trough corrugation and rovibronic coupling modify the rigid free-rotor spectrum.

This observation forces the passage from the scalar
geometric level
\mathcal{L}_{5}
to the electronic-bundle
level
\mathcal{L}_{6}
. The
\mathcal{L}_{5}
projection retains only
the lower adiabatic surface
V_{-}
and the
mass-weighted metric
g
; if the associated nuclear
wavefunction is treated as an ordinary single-valued
function on the pseudorotation circle, this scalar
description predicts the integer sector. The
physical Jahn–Teller problem instead carries a
real ground-state eigenline

L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}\to{C_{e}}(G)\setminus\Sigma_{\mathrm{CI}}

whose first Stiefel–Whitney class

w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})\in H^{1}({C_{e}}(G)\setminus\Sigma_{\mathrm{CI}},\mathbb{Z}/2)

evaluates non-trivially on a meridian loop linking
the CI seam
[
6
]
. This
non-trivial
w_{1}
is the topological datum that
imposes the antiperiodic boundary condition and
shifts the allowed quantum numbers by one half.
The robust discriminator is not a list of fitted
level positions but the boundary condition itself:
periodic versus antiperiodic, an obstruction class
in
\mathbb{Z}/2
that no scalar correction to
V_{-}
can
supply.

The same mathematical invariant also appears in
real Bloch-bundle topology
[
6
]
:
in systems with a real structure,
w_{1}
is the
real-bundle form of a quantised Berry phase. The
molecular and band-theoretic settings have
different base spaces and physical interpretations,
but the underlying real-line-bundle obstruction is
the same. All three Na atoms are equivalent in

\mathrm{Aut}_{\mu}(G)=S_{3}
, so the discrimination involves
no isotope labelling and happens within the
bound-state spectrum of a single chemical species.
Section
8.7
established the
abstract form of this forcing argument; the
remainder of the chapter develops the
\mathcal{L}_{6}

structure required to express, prove, and extend
it. Section
9.1.1
develops the
Mexican-hat Jahn–Teller structure of

\mathrm{Na_{3}}
. Section
9.2

constructs the rank-2 adiabatic sub-bundle and
proves the codimension-2 structure of the CI seam.
Section
9.3
constructs the Berry
connection and proves the holonomy formula

\exp(i\oint A_{0})=-1
. Section
9.4

defines the category
\mathcal{L}_{6}
and the functor

F_{\!6}
. Section
9.6
extends
the framework to ultrafast photodynamics through
CIs. Section
9.7
forces the
further extension to
\mathcal{L}_{7}
.

9.1.1.
\mathrm{Na_{3}}
and the Mexican-hat Jahn–Teller conical intersection

Sodium trimer
\mathrm{Na_{3}}
has molecular graph

G=(\mathrm{Na}_{1},\mathrm{Na}_{2},\mathrm{Na}_{3})

with three equivalent
Z=11
nuclei (each
contributing one
3s
valence electron) and
configuration orbifold
{C_{e}}(G)
of dimension

3(3)-6=3
. Na–Na equilibrium distance is

\sim 3.2
Å. The ground state
X^{2}B_{2}
is
Jahn–Teller distorted from
D_{3h}
equilateral
into an obtuse-isoceles
C_{2v}
structure, with
three equivalent
C_{2v}
geometries related by
cyclic apex permutation. Of interest here is the
electronically excited
2^{2}E^{\prime}
state, accessed by
near-UV absorption.

D_{3h}
degeneracy.

At equilateral
D_{3h}
the
2^{2}E^{\prime}
state belongs
to the two-dimensional
E^{\prime}
irreducible
representation: two electronic states are
degenerate at every
D_{3h}
geometry, so the

2^{2}E^{\prime}
state is a double point. Distortion off
equilateral lifts the degeneracy linearly — the
Jahn–Teller effect. The cheapest distortion is
along the doubly-degenerate
e^{\prime}
vibrational mode
with components
q_{x}
(asymmetric stretch) and

q_{y}
(in-plane bend). The vibronic Hamiltonian
to linear order is

\hat{H}_{\mathrm{JT}}=T_{\mathrm{nuc}}+\tfrac{1}{2}\omega^{2}(q_{x}^{2}+q_{y}^{2})\,\mathbb{1}_{2}+k\bigl(q_{x}\,\sigma_{z}+q_{y}\,\sigma_{x}\bigr),

(25)

acting on the two-component
E^{\prime}
electronic space.
Diagonalisation at each
(q_{x},q_{y})
gives

V_{\pm}(q_{x},q_{y})=\tfrac{1}{2}\omega^{2}(q_{x}^{2}+q_{y}^{2})\pm k\sqrt{q_{x}^{2}+q_{y}^{2}}.

(26)

The lower sheet
V_{-}
has a circular trough at
radius
\rho_{0}=k/\omega^{2}
with a conical
singularity at the origin — the Mexican-hat
potential. Note that
V_{-}
is
not
a Morse
function: its critical locus is the continuous
trough
\rho=\rho_{0}
rather than isolated
non-degenerate critical points, and the central
singularity is a cone rather than a smooth maximum.
The conical intersection
\Sigma_{\mathrm{CI}}
is
the central singular locus at
q_{x}=q_{y}=0
,
parametrised by the totally-symmetric
a_{1}^{\prime}

breathing coordinate.

Codimension of the CI seam.

The
E^{\prime}
degeneracy requires two real conditions

q_{x}=q_{y}=0
in (
25
); hence

\Sigma_{\mathrm{CI}}
is one-dimensional and of
codimension 2 in
{C_{e}}(\mathrm{Na_{3}})
. This is the
canonical real-symmetric codim-2 CI seam to which

w_{1}
is the relevant invariant
(§
9.2
); the seam is
symmetry-required and cannot be removed by
continuous perturbation preserving
D_{3h}
at the
central point.

Labelled branching plane
and the
S_{3}
quotient.

The local
E\otimes e
analysis is carried out on
the
labelled
branching plane
(q_{x},q_{y})\in\mathbb{R}^{2}\setminus\{0\}
, before quotienting by
nuclear permutations. The meridian
\phi:0\to 2\pi
on this labelled plane links the CI seam once
and detects
w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})
. Passing to the

S_{3}
-orbifold quotient identifies the three
equivalent
C_{2v}
minima at
\phi=0,2\pi/3,4\pi/3
but does not remove the local meridian
sign holonomy.
Nuclear exchange-statistical constraints — which classify states by
S_{3}

irreducible representation and select physically allowed combinations of nuclear spin and pseudorotation — are not imposed at
\mathcal{L}_{6}
; they belong to
\mathcal{L}_{7}

(§
9.7
).

Pseudorotation.

On the labelled branching plane, parametrise the
trough by an angle
\phi\in[0,2\pi)
. As
\phi

varies, the molecule passes through the three
equivalent
C_{2v}
structures at
\phi=0,2\pi/3,4\pi/3
as the labelling of which Na atom
sits at the obtuse-isoceles apex cycles by one
position with each increment of
2\pi/3
. This
circulation is
pseudorotation
: the labelling
rotates around the central CI while each atom
undergoes only small periodic displacement.
Higher-order vibronic corrections add a small
three-fold corrugation (
\sim 50
cm
-1
) around
the trough, much smaller than typical vibrational
quanta, so pseudorotation averages over the three

C_{2v}
minima at low excitation.

\mathbb{Z}_{2}
sign holonomy.

In polar coordinates
(q_{x},q_{y})=(\rho\cos\phi,\rho\sin\phi)
, the electronic block of
(
25
) at fixed
\rho=\rho_{0}

becomes
k\rho_{0}(\cos\phi\,\sigma_{z}+\sin\phi\,\sigma_{x})
, with eigenvalues
\pm k\rho_{0}
. One convenient real gauge for the lower
adiabatic eigenline is

|\sigma_{-}(\phi)\rangle\;=\;\sin(\phi/2)\,|1\rangle-\cos(\phi/2)\,|2\rangle,

up to overall sign convention, where
|1\rangle,|2\rangle
span the
E^{\prime}
electronic space at
\phi=0

[
206
,
216
]
. Under
\phi\to\phi+2\pi
the half-angle becomes
\phi/2+\pi
and both trigonometric factors flip sign:

|\sigma_{-}(\phi+2\pi)\rangle=-|\sigma_{-}(\phi)\rangle
. This is the Longuet–Higgins sign-change
theorem for the
E\otimes e
Jahn–Teller system.
The corresponding Berry holonomy is

\exp(i\oint_{\gamma}A_{0})=-1
, the molecular
Aharonov–Bohm effect
[
41
,
216
]
, depending only on the homotopy
class of
\gamma
in
{C_{e}}(\mathrm{Na_{3}})\setminus\Sigma_{\mathrm{CI}}
. Categorically the
\mathbb{Z}_{2}

holonomy is recorded by
w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})
, taking
the value
1\in\mathbb{Z}/2
on every loop linking

\Sigma_{\mathrm{CI}}
(equivalently, sign holonomy

(-1)^{1}=-1
).

Cohomology, codimension, and
invariant

For a smooth (orbi-)manifold
X
, removing a
submanifold
\Sigma
of codimension
d
yields new
cohomology in degree
d-1
:

•

Codim 2
: link is small
S^{1}
,
generating
H_{1}(X\setminus\Sigma)
. Natural

\mathbb{Z}_{2}
-valued invariant of a real line bundle:

w_{1}\in H^{1}(X\setminus\Sigma,\mathbb{Z}/2)
.

•

Codim 3
: link is small
S^{2}
,
generating
H_{2}(X\setminus\Sigma)
. Natural

\mathbb{Z}
-valued invariant of a complex line bundle:

c_{1}\in H^{2}(X\setminus\Sigma,\mathbb{Z})
.

For real-symmetric
\hat{H}_{\mathrm{el}}
,

\Sigma_{\mathrm{CI}}
has codimension 2;

w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})
is the
\mathbb{Z}_{2}
-valued datum that

F_{\!6}
adds to the scalar
\mathcal{L}_{5}
description (Proposition
9.5
).
The complex Chern class
c_{1}(L_{0})\in H^{2}
does not detect
codimension-2 obstructions (which live in
H^{1}
); it becomes
informative only in codim-3 settings (broken TRS, Berry monopoles), where the link is
S^{2}
, a parallel branch of the same construction.

Data progression through the tower.

\underbrace{\mathbb{Z}^{s}}_{\mathcal{L}_{0}}\to\underbrace{\mathbb{R}}_{\mathcal{L}_{1}\text{--}\mathcal{L}_{3}}\to\underbrace{C^{\infty}({C_{e}}(G))}_{\mathcal{L}_{5}}\to\underbrace{H^{1}({C_{e}}(G)\setminus\Sigma_{\mathrm{CI}},\mathbb{Z}/2)}_{\mathcal{L}_{6}\text{ (real, codim 2)}}.

Each step is strictly less deformable than the
previous; a
\mathbb{Z}_{2}
invariant changes only in discrete steps.

Why
\mathbb{Z}_{2}
-valuedness matters chemically

w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})
is a topologically protected
property of a molecule’s electronic structure,
unlike
V^{\ddagger}
or
\Delta G
which vary
continuously with substitution, solvent, or
temperature. Along any closed loop of
configurations
w_{1}
takes the value
0
(no CI
enclosed) or
1
(odd number of CI components
enclosed); there is no “half a conical
intersection”. Continuous perturbations cannot
turn a CI on or off gradually — the gap either
closes along the path (
w_{1}
flips) or it does not.
This discreteness makes CI topology experimentally
certifiable: a
\pm
outcome on each loop-resolved
measurement, not a continuous number to fit.

Forcing pair for
\mathcal{L}_{6}
: integer
vs. half-integer pseudorotation quanta of

\mathrm{Na_{3}}

Setup.

G=\mathrm{Na_{3}}
with configuration orbifold

{C_{e}}(\mathrm{Na_{3}})
and metric
g
fixed. The
Mexican-hat lower-sheet surface
V_{-}
from
(
26
) (with small three-fold
corrugation) is common to the two descriptions
below;
I_{\mathrm{ps}}
is determined by
V_{-}
and

g
. The
\mathcal{L}_{5}
functor
F_{\!V}
retains only the
scalar pair
(V_{-},g)
on

{C_{e}}(\mathrm{Na_{3}})\setminus\Sigma_{\mathrm{CI}}

and produces the same
\mathcal{L}_{5}
image in both
descriptions.

Description A (
\mathcal{L}_{5}
:
single-valued nuclear wavefunction).

The nuclear wavefunction is an ordinary function on

{C_{e}}(\mathrm{Na_{3}})\setminus\Sigma_{\mathrm{CI}}

(section of the trivial real line bundle); the
Mead–Truhlar connection is set to zero. The
pseudorotation Hamiltonian

\hat{H}_{\mathrm{ps}}^{(A)}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2I_{\mathrm{ps}}}\frac{\partial^{2}}{\partial\phi^{2}}+V_{\mathrm{trough}}(\phi),\qquad\psi(\phi+2\pi)=\psi(\phi),

has eigenvalues

E_{j}^{(A)}\approx\hbar^{2}j^{2}/(2I_{\mathrm{ps}})

with
j=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,\ldots
in the
free-pseudorotor limit; lowest level at
j=0
.

Description B (
\mathcal{L}_{6}
:
real sub-bundle with
w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})=1
).

The nuclear wavefunction is a section of

L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}
with
w_{1}=1
on every pseudorotation
loop — equivalently, a function on the double
cover, antiperiodic under the deck transformation

\psi(\phi+2\pi)=-\psi(\phi)
. Same operator

\hat{H}_{\mathrm{ps}}
, enlarged function space;
eigenvalues

E_{j}^{(B)}\approx\hbar^{2}j^{2}/(2I_{\mathrm{ps}})

with
j=\pm 1/2,\pm 3/2,\pm 5/2,\ldots
in the
free-pseudorotor limit; lowest level at
j=\pm 1/2
with zero-point energy

\hbar^{2}/(8I_{\mathrm{ps}})
above the trough bottom.
No
j=0
level exists in this topological sector.

Empirical anchor.

The 1986 measurement of the
2^{2}E^{\prime}
state by R2PI
on cold supersonic-beam

\mathrm{Na_{3}}

[
75
]

resolves the vibrational structure consistent with
the half-integer pseudorotational assignment.
Quantitative corrections from trough corrugation
and rovibronic coupling modify the rigid free-rotor
spacings, but the topological boundary condition
distinguishing A from B remains the robust
datum
[
213
,
217
]
.

Non-trivial fibre of

U_{6\to 5}
.

Descriptions A and B are two distinct lifts of the
same
\mathcal{L}_{5}
object
({C_{e}}(\mathrm{Na_{3}}),V_{-},g)

under the forgetful projection

U_{6\to 5}:\mathcal{L}_{6}\longrightarrow\mathcal{L}_{5}.

The fibre
U_{6\to 5}^{-1}(V_{-},g)
is non-trivial:
one lift carries trivial real eigenline monodromy
(
w_{1}=0
), the physical Jahn–Teller lift carries

w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})\neq 0
. The
\mathcal{L}_{5}
image does
not contain enough data to select between them; the

w_{1}
. The purely scalar, single-valued
\mathcal{L}_{5}

description is therefore empirically insufficient
for this spectrum: the
\mathcal{L}_{6}
lift with non-trivial

w_{1}
supplies the missing boundary condition.

Three qualitative failures
of the
\mathcal{L}_{5}
description.

(i)
Boundary condition:

\mathcal{L}_{5}
enforces
periodicity
\psi(\phi+2\pi)=\psi(\phi)
by
treating
\psi
as a single-valued function on the
pseudorotation circle; the physical eigenstate is
antiperiodic.
(ii)
Lowest level:

\mathcal{L}_{5}
predicts a

j=0
ground state at the trough bottom; the

\mathcal{L}_{6}
lift and experiment exclude this level,
the spectrum starting at
j=\pm 1/2
.
(iii)
Non-adiabatic coupling:

d_{01}^{\mu}=\langle\sigma_{-}|\partial_{\mu}\hat{H}_{\mathrm{el}}|\sigma_{+}\rangle/(V_{+}-V_{-})
diverges as

\mathbf{R}\to\Sigma_{\mathrm{CI}}
; single-surface
Born–Oppenheimer breaks down at the
CI
[
283
,
190
,
161
,
65
]
.
The rank-2 adiabatic sub-bundle is the natural

\mathcal{L}_{6}
object.

None of (i)–(iii) is a quantitative correction:
each is a topological feature of the
\mathcal{L}_{6}
lift
that no continuous adjustment of the scalar
V_{-}

supplies. Antiperiodicity is a
\mathbb{Z}_{2}
obstruction
class, not a numerical parameter.

The three failures identify the new data
\mathcal{L}_{6}

carries: the codimension-2 CI seam

\Sigma_{\mathrm{CI}}\subset{C_{e}}(G)

(§
9.2
), the Berry connection
A_{0}

on
L_{0}
with real-gauge sign holonomy on

L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}
(§

), and the
codimension-matched invariants
w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})\in H^{1}(\cdot,\mathbb{Z}/2)
(real-symmetric, codim-2) and

c_{1}(L_{0})\in H^{2}(\cdot,\mathbb{Z})
(broken-TRS,

(§

).

Scattering corroboration in

\mathrm{H}+\mathrm{HD}

The same

bundle structure appears in
reactive scattering. H
3
shares the

Jahn–Teller

structure of

\mathrm{Na_{3}}

resolve forward-scattering oscillations in

[

]
; the analogous
effect below the CI was reported
in

]
. Single-surface

\mathcal{L}_{5}

[

]
predicts smooth angular

boundary

reproduces the oscillations

[

]
. The
topological sign comes from the electronic CI of

3
system; the H/D substitution makes

and changes the scattering kinematics, but the

holonomy associated with loops around the H

\mathrm{Na_{3}}

and reactive scattering of

are two manifestations of the same

holonomy in different observable channels.

§9.2. The full electronic Hilbert bundle and the conical intersection seam

9.2.1. From a scalar surface to an electronic bundle

At
\mathcal{L}_{5}
, the electronic structure of a molecular graph
G
is retained only through its scalar adiabatic shadow: a potential-energy surface
V_{0}:\Omega\subset{C_{e}}(G)\to\mathbb{R}
and the mass-weighted metric
g
.
In the clamped-nuclei Born–Oppenheimer setting,

V_{0}(\mathbf{R})\;=\;E_{\rm el,0}(\mathbf{R})+V_{\rm nn}(\mathbf{R}),

where
E_{\rm el,0}
is the lowest eigenvalue of the electronic Hamiltonian
\hat{H}_{\rm el}(\mathbf{R})
and
V_{\rm nn}
is the nuclear–nuclear repulsion.
Section
9.1
showed that the
scalar shadow is qualitatively incomplete in the presence of a Jahn–Teller / conical-intersection sign effect; the missing datum is the topology of the real ground-state eigenline.
The minimal extension carries, at each
\mathbf{R}
, the
N
-dimensional spectral subspace of the lowest
N\geq 2
states of
\hat{H}_{\rm el}
, well-defined as a whole under internal degeneracies provided the
N
-th level remains spectrally isolated from the
(N+1)
-st.

Definition 9.1

(Rank-
N
adiabatic bundle)
.

Let
G\in\mathbf{LGraph}_{P}
and
N\geq 2
. Let
\Omega\subset{C_{e}}(G)
be an open adiabatic region on which
E_{N}(\mathbf{R})-E_{N-1}(\mathbf{R})\geq\Delta>0
.
Let

P_{N}(\mathbf{R})\;=\;\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{\Gamma(\mathbf{R})}\bigl(z-\hat{H}_{\rm el}(\mathbf{R})\bigr)^{-1}\,dz

be the Riesz spectral projector onto the lowest
N
states, with
\Gamma(\mathbf{R})
a smooth contour separating
\{E_{0},\ldots,E_{N-1}\}
from the rest of the spectrum.
The
rank-
N
adiabatic bundle
is

\pi:{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(N)}\to\Omega,\qquad{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(N)}_{\mathbf{R}}:=\operatorname{Ran}P_{N}(\mathbf{R}),

a smooth Hermitian vector bundle of rank
N
with structure group
U(N)
, well-defined even under internal degeneracies because the spectral subspace is isolated from the
(N+1)
-st state on
\Omega

[
283
]
.

On the non-degenerate locus
\Omega^{\circ}:=\Omega\setminus\mathcal{X}_{01}
(where
E_{0}<E_{1}
), the ground-state eigenline
L_{0}\to\Omega^{\circ}
is the smooth complex line sub-bundle with fibre
\ker(\hat{H}_{\rm el}(\mathbf{R})-E_{0}(\mathbf{R}))
.
In the real time-reversal-symmetric case (
\hat{H}_{\rm el}^{\top}=\hat{H}_{\rm el}
in a real basis),
L_{0}
carries a canonical real form
L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}\to\Omega^{\circ}
with structure group
O(1)=\{\pm 1\}
.
Its first Stiefel–Whitney class

w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})\;\in\;H^{1}(\Omega^{\circ};\,\mathbb{Z}/2)

is the categorical invariant the
\mathcal{L}_{6}
level adds to the
\mathcal{L}_{5}
scalar data: for any loop
\gamma\subset\Omega^{\circ}
the observable sign holonomy of the real eigenline is

\operatorname{Hol}_{L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}}(\gamma)\;=\;(-1)^{\langle w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}),[\gamma]\rangle}\;\in\;\{\pm 1\}.

The complex Chern class
c_{1}(L_{0})\in H^{2}(\Omega^{\circ};\mathbb{Z})
vanishes in the real-symmetric case; it becomes informative only when time-reversal symmetry is broken, where the degeneracy locus has codimension
3
and the link is
S^{2}
.
An
\mathcal{L}_{6}
lift accordingly records the tuple

\bigl(\Omega,\,{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(N)},\,A,\,\mathcal{X}_{01},\,w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})\bigr),

comprising the active region, rank-
N
active bundle, Berry connection
A
, CI seam, and Stiefel–Whitney class of the real ground-state eigenline.

9.2.2. The conical intersection seam

Definition 9.2

(Conical intersection seam)
.

Let
\Omega\subset{C_{e}}(G)
be an adiabatic region with an isolated rank-
2
active subspace
{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(2)}
.
The
conical intersection seam
between the two lowest states is

\mathcal{X}_{01}\;:=\;\bigl\{\,\mathbf{R}\in\Omega\;\big|\;E_{0}(\mathbf{R})=E_{1}(\mathbf{R}),\ \text{regular conical at }\mathbf{R}\,\bigr\}.

At
\mathbf{R}_{0}\in\mathcal{X}_{01}
, in a local smooth frame of
{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(2)}
, the traceless effective two-state Hamiltonian in the real time-reversal-symmetric case takes the form

H_{\rm eff}^{0}(\mathbf{R})\;=\;x(\mathbf{R})\,\sigma_{z}+y(\mathbf{R})\,\sigma_{x},

with
x,y
smooth real functions.
The degeneracy is
regular conical
if
dx_{\mathbf{R}_{0}},dy_{\mathbf{R}_{0}}
are linearly independent in
T^{*}_{\mathbf{R}_{0}}\Omega
; equivalently, the local gap is
E_{1}-E_{0}=2\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}+O(|(x,y)|^{2})
.
The covectors
dx,dy
are the gradient-difference and derivative-coupling directions in a branching-plane representation
[
312
,
79
]
; the rank condition is invariant although individual covectors are not.
Adiabatic eigenvectors
\sigma_{0},\sigma_{1}
are not canonically defined at
\mathbf{R}_{0}
— only the two-dimensional spectral subspace
{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(2)}_{\mathbf{R}_{0}}
is.

Proposition 9.3

(CI seam has codimension 2)
.

Let
G
have
f=3n-6\geq 3
internal degrees of freedom and let
\hat{H}_{\rm el}
be real-symmetric on
\Omega
.
For a generic
\hat{H}_{\rm el}
, the regular part of
\mathcal{X}_{01}
is a smooth submanifold of codimension
2
in
\Omega
, of dimension
f-2
; non-regular points form a closed subset of positive codimension within
\mathcal{X}_{01}
.

Proof.

The traceless two-state model
H_{\rm eff}^{0}=x\sigma_{z}+y\sigma_{x}
has gap
2\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}
, so degeneracy requires
x=y=0
: two independent real conditions.
At a regular point,
dx,dy
are linearly independent and the implicit function theorem gives a codimension-
2
submanifold.
Non-regular points form a closed positive-codimension subset by genericity
[
292
]
.
For complex Hermitian
\hat{H}_{\rm el}
, the traceless two-state model is
x\sigma_{x}+y\sigma_{y}+z\sigma_{z}
, requiring three independent real conditions, so
\codim(\mathcal{X}_{01})=3
.
∎

Remark 9.4

(Local model and half-angle sign change)
.

In polar coordinates
(q_{x},q_{y})=(\rho\cos\phi,\rho\sin\phi)
, the local model
H_{\rm eff}^{0}=q_{x}\sigma_{z}+q_{y}\sigma_{x}
has a real lower-state eigenvector depending on the half-angle
\phi/2
that flips sign under
\phi\mapsto\phi+2\pi
— the Longuet–Higgins sign change
[
206
]
.
In bundle language,
\langle w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}),[S^{1}_{\rm mer}]\rangle=1
: the real codim-
2
CI is detected by Stiefel–Whitney on a meridian
loop
, not by a Chern class on a meridian sphere.

Codimension 2 picks out
H^{1}
and
w_{1}

A codimension-
d
submanifold
\Sigma\subset X
has small normal link
S^{d-1}
, so topological obstructions in
X\setminus\Sigma
live in cohomology of degree
d-1
.

For a real time-reversal-symmetric CI,
\mathcal{X}_{01}
has codimension
2
and link
S^{1}
; the invariant is
w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})\in H^{1}(X\setminus\mathcal{X}_{01};\mathbb{Z}/2)
,
and pairing with the meridian gives the Longuet–Higgins sign change.
For broken time-reversal symmetry, the seam has codimension
3
, link
S^{2}
, and invariant
c_{1}\in H^{2}
.
The two cases are parallel branches of the same

\mathcal{L}_{6}
construction; thermal molecular chemistry inhabits the
w_{1}
branch.

9.2.3. The Stiefel–Whitney invariant and holonomy

Proposition 9.5

(Meridian loops and the
\mathcal{L}_{6}
invariant)
.

Let
\mathcal{X}_{01}\subset X\subset{C_{e}}(G)
be a regular codimension-
2
CI seam for a real-symmetric Hamiltonian, and let
X^{\circ}:=X\setminus\mathcal{X}_{01}
. Then:

(i)

Each connected component of
\mathcal{X}_{01}

contributes one
\mathbb{Z}/2
generator to

H^{1}(X^{\circ};\mathbb{Z}/2)
, dual to a small meridian loop
S^{1}
.

(ii)

The first Stiefel–Whitney class of

L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}
evaluates to
1\in\mathbb{Z}/2
on every such meridian.

(iii)

For any loop
\gamma\subset X^{\circ}
,

\operatorname{Hol}_{L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}}(\gamma)\;=\;(-1)^{\langle w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}),[\gamma]\rangle}\;=\;(-1)^{\operatorname{lk}_{2}(\gamma,\mathcal{X}_{01})},

with
\operatorname{lk}_{2}(\gamma,\mathcal{X}_{01})\in\mathbb{Z}/2
the mod-
2
linking number.

Proof.

(i) follows from the mod-
2
Thom–Gysin sequence for the closed codim-
2
submanifold
\mathcal{X}_{01}\subset X
: one
\mathbb{Z}/2
generator per connected component, dual to a meridian loop.

(ii) is Remark
9.4
: in the normal slice, the real lower-state eigenvector flips sign under
\phi\mapsto\phi+2\pi
, so
\langle w_{1},[S^{1}_{\rm mer}]\rangle=1
; the result extends to all meridians by homotopy invariance.

(iii) The holonomy of a real line bundle around a loop is by definition
(-1)^{\langle w_{1},[\gamma]\rangle}
. For
\gamma\subset X^{\circ}
, the pairing equals the mod-
2
count of transverse intersections of any spanning chain with
\mathcal{X}_{01}
, which is
\operatorname{lk}_{2}(\gamma,\mathcal{X}_{01})
.
∎

The proposition makes the
\mathcal{L}_{5}
vs.
\mathcal{L}_{6}
distinction explicit.
An avoided crossing has
\mathcal{X}_{01}=\emptyset
and
L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}
extends as a smooth real line bundle over
\Omega
with finite derivative coupling.
A regular CI has non-empty
\mathcal{X}_{01}
and non-trivial sign holonomy on meridians.
The scalar
\mathcal{L}_{5}
datum cannot distinguish these cases — both produce the same
V_{0}
on the accessible region — but
\mathcal{L}_{6}
does, through the
\mathbb{Z}/2
class
w_{1}
.

9.2.4. The forgetful functor
U_{6}

The
U_{6}
diagram

The level-to-level forgetful functor
U_{6}:\mathcal{L}_{6}(P)\to\mathcal{L}_{5}(P)
is characterised by the commutative square

where
\mathbf{For}
sends

(\Omega,{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(N)},A,\mathcal{X}_{01},w_{1})\mapsto(\Omega,V_{0},g)
, retaining the scalar adiabatic shadow and discarding the bundle data.
Commutativity
\mathbf{For}\circ F_{\!6}=F_{\!V}\circ U_{6}
expresses Layer 2(b) consistency: the ground-state surface retained by
U_{6}
equals the scalar shadow recorded by
F_{\!V}
.

The Na
3
forcing example (§
9.1
) is a non-faithfulness statement for
U_{6}
: the scalar lower-sheet description
(\Omega,V_{-},g)
admits two distinct lifts,

trivial:

\displaystyle(G,{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(N)},A,\mathcal{X}_{01},w_{1}=0),

Jahn–Teller:

\displaystyle(G,{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(N)},A,\mathcal{X}_{01},w_{1}\neq 0),

with the same
\mathcal{L}_{5}
image.
The fibre
U_{6}^{-1}(\Omega,V_{-},g)
is non-trivial.
The trivial lift is a comparison object, not a second physical Hamiltonian: it makes the failure of
U_{6}
to be an equivalence explicit.

§9.3. Berry connection, sign holonomy, and the
topological phase

Section
9.2
established the rank-
N

adiabatic bundle
{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(N)}\to\Omega
, located the
CI seam
\mathcal{X}_{01}
as the codimension-
2
degeneracy
locus, and identified the categorical invariant of
the
\mathcal{L}_{6}
level as the first Stiefel–Whitney class

w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})\in H^{1}(\Omega^{\circ};\mathbb{Z}/2)
of the
real ground-state eigenline. This section develops
the analytic representation of that invariant in
terms of a Berry connection, fixes the gauge story
in the real-symmetric case, and exhibits the sign
holonomy as the
\mathcal{L}_{6}
datum that the scalar
\mathcal{L}_{5}

shadow cannot supply.

9.3.1. The Berry connection

The Berry connection on the chosen active spectral
bundle
{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(N)}\to\Omega
is the projected
connection

\nabla^{\rm B}\;=\;P_{N}\,d,

induced by projecting the trivial Hilbert-space
connection with the Riesz projector
P_{N}
of
Definition
9.1
. In a local
orthonormal frame
\{\sigma_{k}\}_{k=0}^{N-1}
, its
matrix elements are
[
41
,
300
,
283
]

A_{kl}^{\mu}(\mathbf{R})\;=\;i\,\langle\sigma_{k}(\mathbf{R})\,|\,\partial_{\mu}\,\sigma_{l}(\mathbf{R})\rangle.

The construction depends on the choice of active
projector
P_{N}
. Under a smooth gauge transformation

\sigma_{k}\mapsto\sum_{j}U_{jk}\,\sigma_{j}
with

U:\Omega\to U(N)
, the connection transforms by
the standard rule

A\;\mapsto\;U^{\dagger}AU+i\,U^{\dagger}dU.

On the non-degenerate locus
\Omega^{\circ}:=\Omega\setminus\mathcal{X}_{01}
where the ground-state eigenline

L_{0}\subset{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(N)}
is a smooth rank-one
sub-bundle, the abelian Berry connection on
L_{0}
is
the restriction

A_{0}^{\mu}(\mathbf{R})\;=\;i\,\langle\sigma_{0}(\mathbf{R})\,|\,\partial_{\mu}\,\sigma_{0}(\mathbf{R})\rangle.

9.3.2. Real Hamiltonians: local vanishing
and global monodromy

For real-symmetric
\hat{H}_{\rm el}
the abelian
Berry connection vanishes locally in any real gauge.
The non-trivial
\mathcal{L}_{6}
topology is encoded entirely
in the failure of any real gauge to extend
single-valuedly around loops linking
\mathcal{X}_{01}
.

Proposition 9.6

(Local vanishing of
A_{0}
in a
real gauge)
.

Let
\hat{H}_{\rm el}
be real-symmetric on
\Omega
,
and let
\sigma_{0}(\mathbf{R})
be a smooth real
normalised ground-state eigenvector on a
contractible open patch
U\subset\Omega^{\circ}
.
Then

A_{0}\;=\;i\,\langle\sigma_{0}|d\sigma_{0}\rangle\;=\;0\qquad\text{on }U.

Proof.

Since
\sigma_{0}
is real-valued in the chosen real
basis,
\langle a|b\rangle=\langle b|a\rangle

for any real
a,b
, so

0\;=\;d\,\langle\sigma_{0}|\sigma_{0}\rangle\;=\;\langle d\sigma_{0}|\sigma_{0}\rangle+\langle\sigma_{0}|d\sigma_{0}\rangle\;=\;2\,\langle\sigma_{0}|d\sigma_{0}\rangle.

Hence
\langle\sigma_{0}|d\sigma_{0}\rangle=0
and
therefore
A_{0}=0
identically on
U
.
∎

Proposition 9.7

(Half-angle gauge and meridian
monodromy)
.

In the local two-state model
H_{\rm eff}^{0}(q_{x},q_{y})=q_{x}\sigma_{z}+q_{y}\sigma_{x}
on a normal slice
to
\mathcal{X}_{01}
, write
q_{x}=\rho\cos\phi
,
q_{y}=\rho\sin\phi
. A real lower-state eigenvector may
be chosen as

\sigma_{0}(\phi)\;=\;\sin(\phi/2)\,|1\rangle-\cos(\phi/2)\,|2\rangle,

for which
A_{0}=0
on any simply connected

\phi
-patch by
Proposition
9.6
. Under
\phi\mapsto\phi+2\pi
,

\sigma_{0}(\phi+2\pi)\;=\;-\,\sigma_{0}(\phi).

The transition function around the meridian loop is
therefore
-1
; equivalently, the
O(1)
-holonomy
of
L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}
around the meridian is
-1
and

\langle w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}),[S^{1}_{\rm mer}]\rangle\;=\;1.

Proof.

The eigenvector identity follows from the local
model (Remark
9.4
of
§
9.2
). Vanishing of
A_{0}
is
Proposition
9.6
. The sign
change is direct:
\sin(\phi/2+\pi)=-\sin(\phi/2)
and
\cos(\phi/2+\pi)=-\cos(\phi/2)
.
∎

For the
E\otimes e
Jahn–Teller model
of
\mathrm{Na_{3}}
, the pseudorotation loop is
precisely such a meridian loop in the branching
plane, so the above sign holonomy is the
topological origin of the half-integer
pseudorotation quantum numbers established in
§
9.1
.

Remark 9.8

(Singular
U(1)
representation of the
same holonomy)
.

The sign holonomy can also be represented in a
singular complex gauge. Define

\tilde{\sigma}_{0}(\phi)\;:=\;e^{i\phi/2}\,\sigma_{0}(\phi),

which is single-valued:
\tilde{\sigma}_{0}(\phi+2\pi)=e^{i\pi}\cdot(-\sigma_{0}(\phi))=\tilde{\sigma}_{0}(\phi)
. With the convention
A=i\langle\sigma|d\sigma\rangle
used throughout
this section, a direct computation gives

\tilde{A}_{0}\;=\;i\,\langle\tilde{\sigma}_{0}|d\tilde{\sigma}_{0}\rangle\;=\;-\tfrac{1}{2}\,d\phi,

so
\oint_{S^{1}_{\rm mer}}\tilde{A}_{0}=-\pi
.
Changing the sign convention for the Berry
connection reverses this sign, but the holonomy

\exp(i\oint\tilde{A}_{0})=-1
is unchanged and is
the only convention-independent statement. This

U(1)
representation should not be confused with a
half-integer first Chern class:
L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}
is a
real line bundle with structure group
O(1)
, and
the
\pm 1
is its mod-
2
monodromy. The

\pm 1/2
in the singular gauge is an artefact of
representing
O(1)
inside
U(1)
, not the value of
an integer characteristic class.

9.3.3. Berry curvature on the complement of
the seam

Definition 9.9

(Berry curvature)
.

The
Berry curvature
of the abelian
connection on
L_{0}\to\Omega^{\circ}
is the
gauge-invariant
2
-form
\Omega_{0}=dA_{0}
. In
second-order perturbation theory,

\Omega_{0}^{\mu\nu}(\mathbf{R})\;=\;-2\,\mathrm{Im}\!\sum_{k}\frac{\langle\sigma_{0}|\partial_{\mu}\hat{H}_{\rm el}|\sigma_{k}\rangle\,\langle\sigma_{k}|\partial_{\nu}\hat{H}_{\rm el}|\sigma_{0}\rangle}{(E_{k}-E_{0})^{2}},

where the sum runs over excited states in the
chosen spectral resolution. For the exact
ground-state eigenline, the sum is over all
k\geq 1
; in an
N
-state truncated model the same
formula holds after projection onto the active
subspace, with truncation error inherent in the
model choice
[
41
,
300
]
.

Proposition 9.10

(Real-symmetric curvature
vanishes pointwise)
.

If
\hat{H}_{\rm el}
is real-symmetric, then

\Omega_{0}=0
pointwise on
\Omega^{\circ}
.

Proof.

With
\hat{H}_{\rm el}
real-symmetric in a real
basis, all matrix elements

\langle\sigma_{0}|\partial_{\mu}\hat{H}_{\rm el}|\sigma_{k}\rangle
are real, so each summand in
the perturbative formula is real and the imaginary
part vanishes. Equivalently, by
Proposition
9.6
,
A_{0}=0

locally in a real gauge, hence
\Omega_{0}=dA_{0}=0
.
∎

Remark 9.11

(Distributional “
\pi
-flux”
picture and derivative coupling)
.

In the singular complex gauge of
Remark
9.8
,
\tilde{A}_{0}=-\tfrac{1}{2}d\phi
has vanishing exterior derivative
on
\Omega^{\circ}
but is not exact there; the

-\pi
holonomy on a meridian is sometimes written
as a
\pm\pi
delta-flux supported on
\mathcal{X}_{01}
.
This is a useful physicist’s heuristic, but the
gauge-free formulation of the obstruction is the

\mathbb{Z}/2
class
w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})
. Away from the
seam, the derivative coupling

\tau_{01}^{\mu}\;:=\;\langle\sigma_{0}|\partial_{\mu}\sigma_{1}\rangle

has the standard perturbative form

\tau_{01}^{\mu}\;=\;\frac{\langle\sigma_{0}|\partial_{\mu}\hat{H}_{\rm el}|\sigma_{1}\rangle}{E_{1}-E_{0}}

(up to the usual sign convention for state
ordering). It is finite on
\Omega^{\circ}
and
diverges as
\mathbf{R}\to\mathcal{X}_{01}
, signalling the
breakdown of single-state adiabatic
dynamics
[
283
]
.

9.3.4. Sign holonomy and the topological
invariant

Definition 9.12

(Berry sign and Berry phase)
.

For a real-symmetric
\hat{H}_{\rm el}
on
\Omega
,
let
\eta_{B}:=w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})\in H^{1}(\Omega^{\circ};\mathbb{Z}/2)
. For a loop
\gamma\subset\Omega^{\circ}
,
the
Berry sign
is the holonomy of the real
eigenline

\operatorname{Hol}_{L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}}(\gamma)\;=\;(-1)^{\langle\eta_{B},[\gamma]\rangle}\;\in\;\{+1,-1\}.

In the singular
U(1)
representation of
Remark
9.8
, this corresponds to a
Berry phase class

[\gamma_{B}(\gamma)]\;=\;\pi\,\langle\eta_{B},[\gamma]\rangle\pmod{2\pi},

taking values in
\{0,\pi\}
.

Proposition 9.13

(Sign holonomy and mod-
2

linking)
.

Assume that on the region
\Omega
under
consideration
w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}})
is the mod-
2

Poincaré dual of the regular CI seam
\mathcal{X}_{01}
(this
holds locally near a regular seam by the Thom-Gysin
construction of
Proposition
9.5
). Let
\gamma\subset\Omega^{\circ}
be a loop bounding a

2
-chain
C\subset\Omega
transverse to

\mathcal{X}_{01}
. Then

\langle w_{1}(L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}),[\gamma]\rangle\;=\;\#(C\cap\mathcal{X}_{01})\pmod{2},

and equivalently

\operatorname{Hol}_{L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}}(\gamma)\;=\;(-1)^{\operatorname{lk}_{2}(\gamma,\mathcal{X}_{01})}.

Proof.

This is Proposition
9.5
(iii) of
§
9.2
restated under the
Poincaré-duality hypothesis:
w_{1}
pairs with

[\gamma]\in H_{1}(\Omega^{\circ};\mathbb{Z}/2)
to give the
mod-
2
intersection number of any spanning chain
with
\mathcal{X}_{01}
. Independence of the choice of
C

follows under the stated hypothesis; locally in a
tubular neighbourhood of a regular seam, this is
the standard meridian computation.
∎

Proposition 9.14

(Reconciliation with the
\mathcal{L}_{5}

shadow)
.

If the real eigenline
L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}\to\Omega
is
orientable — for example, if
\Omega
is simply
connected and the ground state is non-degenerate
and gapped on
\Omega
— then a global real gauge
can be chosen, the abelian Berry connection
vanishes globally, and every sign holonomy is
+1
.
If
\Omega^{\circ}
contains a regular CI seam and

\gamma

\langle w_{1},[\gamma]\rangle=1
and

\operatorname{Hol}_{L_{0}^{\mathbb{R}}}(\gamma)=-1
. The
scalar
\mathcal{L}_{5}
shadow
(\Omega,V_{0},g)
does not
by itself determine the topology of the real

\Omega^{\circ}
, nor the
corresponding nuclear boundary condition; the

\mathcal{L}_{6}
datum is the
w_{1}
-class. In the

3
forcing example of
§
9.1
, forgetting the eigenline
topology leaves the same lower-sheet
pseudorotational scalar shape but loses the
antiperiodic boundary condition: quantising the
scalar shadow with single-valued nuclear
wavefunctions gives the integer sector, while
restoring
w_{1}\neq 0
gives the physical
half-integer sector.

The
\mathcal{L}_{6}
invariant chain

In a singular complex gauge the same sign is
written as a Berry phase
0
or
\pi
modulo

2\pi
; the two presentations describe the same

O(1)
holonomy class. The
\mathbb{Z}/2
value is the

\mathcal{L}_{6}
topological datum discarded by the
forgetful functor
U_{6}:\mathcal{L}_{6}(P)\to\mathcal{L}_{5}(P)
.

§9.4. Definition of

Sections

For a loop

the

9.4.1. Target categories: scalar shadow and electronic bundle

Two target categories are needed: a scalar target
\mathbf{Scal}^{\mathrm{Geom}}

\mathcal{L}_{6}
