What the
\mathcal{L}_{7}
chapter contributes

Three contributions distinguish the tower at
\mathcal{L}_{7}
.

Forcing-pair discipline.

Table
4
records a concrete reaction
pair justifying each transition
\mathcal{L}_{k-1}\to\mathcal{L}_{k}
; the
tower is built from the bottom upward by this discipline
rather than designed from the top downward.
To our knowledge, no prior categorical treatment of chemistry
(Baez–Fong, Baez–Pollard, Coecke) proceeds by forcing
pairs; in those we are aware of, the mathematical structure is
chosen first and chemistry mapped into it.
The forcing-pair discipline is a methodological contribution,
not a theorem.

Para enrichment as a separate dimension.

Every level
\mathcal{L}_{k}
carries a Para shadow

\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}
of parametric equivariant maps, in the sense of Gavranović et al.
[
114
]
.
Machine-learning models for chemistry —
yield predictors, neural ODEs, equivariant force fields,
learned wavefunctions, VQE — are lax algebra morphisms in

\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}
, and their equivariance and
thermodynamic-consistency constraints follow from universal
properties of the Para construction rather than from
architectural choices.
Developed in Chapter
11
.

Open problems precisely formulated.

The four conjectures of §
10.6
give a
precise categorical formulation of what is needed to
make the Born–Oppenheimer approximation, the topology of
conical intersections, and the emergence of molecular
identity into rigorous theorems about a single categorical
object
\mathcal{L}_{7}(P)
.
The mathematical tools exist in pieces (PST, Landsman,
Georgescu, Renault, Amann); their assembly into the
constructions C1–C4 is the research programme.

The tower does not claim that quantum chemistry is

solved
at
\mathcal{L}_{7}
.
It claims that a precise mathematical object to carry
quantum chemistry has been defined, its content layers
identified, and the constructions that would produce
specific instances stated precisely enough to be either
completed or refuted.

§11. The Para Enrichment: Machine Learning Models and
Categorical Completeness

The exact tower
\mathcal{L}_{0}(P)\hookrightarrow\cdots\hookrightarrow\mathcal{L}_{7}(P)
built in Chapters
2
–
10
is the
structural decomposition of chemistry developed in this
monograph:
species and stoichiometry at
\mathcal{L}_{0}
,
enthalpy additivity at
\mathcal{L}_{1}
,
the dagger and detailed balance at
\mathcal{L}_{2}
,
the chemical master equation at
\mathcal{L}_{3}
,
bond topology at
\mathcal{L}_{4}
,
stereochemistry at
\mathcal{L}_{4.5}
,
the Born–Oppenheimer potential at
\mathcal{L}_{5}
,
electronic structure at
\mathcal{L}_{6}
,
and nuclear quantisation at
\mathcal{L}_{7}
.
Each morphism in the tower is an exact law.
Each extension was forced by a reaction pair the level below could
not distinguish.
Nothing in that construction was statistical;
nothing was learned from data.

This chapter turns the tower outward.
The models used to compute chemistry in practice today —
MACE
[
34
]
, NequIP
[
37
]
,
So3krates
[
100
]
, SO3LR
[
160
]
,
QIM
[
89
]
, and the rest of the published molecular
machine learning catalogue — are neural networks, trained force
fields, parametric surrogates.
The question this chapter asks is what the tower, as a completed
structural object, tells us about these models:
what their architectures already commit to,
what they can and cannot represent,
which tower-coherence conditions they silently respect or silently
violate.

A direct answer is blocked by a categorical kind mismatch.
A tower morphism at level
k
is an exact map: one specific,
deterministic morphism of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
, delivered once and for
all by the tower construction of Chapters
2
–
10
.
A MACE force field is a parametric family

\{f_{\theta}\}_{\theta\in\Theta}
, one map per point in a weight
space
\Theta
that the training procedure selects from.
The two sit in different kinds of category:
tower morphisms in hom-sets
\mathcal{C}(X,Y)
,
MACE in something like

\coprod_{\Theta}\mathcal{C}(\Theta\otimes X,Y)
.
Asking “which tower level does MACE occupy?” is a category error
in the literal sense;
the tower and the MACE model are different kinds of mathematical
object and share no hom-set.
To use the tower as a diagnostic for the ML literature, we need a
categorical setting in which parametric families and exact morphisms
both live, with the exact tower appearing as a distinguished
sub-structure of the richer whole.

The construction that does this is the
Para 2-category
of
Gavranović et al.
[
112
]
.
For a symmetric monoidal category
(\mathcal{C},\otimes,I)
, the
2-category
\mathrm{Para}(\mathcal{C})
has the same objects as
\mathcal{C}
,
but its 1-morphisms
X\to Y
are pairs
(\Theta,f_{\theta})
with

\Theta\in\mathcal{C}
a parameter space and

f_{\theta}\colon\Theta\otimes X\to Y
a morphism of
\mathcal{C}
.
2-morphisms are
reparametrisations

r\colon\Theta^{\prime}\to\Theta
, encoding weight tying, fine-tuning, and transfer learning.
Applied at each tower level, Para produces a
perpendicular
enrichment

\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
:
a 2-category of parametric morphisms standing above the exact
morphisms of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
, with a vertical embedding
\gamma_{k}

placing each exact law as its trivial-parameter (
\Theta=I
)
version.
There is no canonical reverse functor collapsing a parametric
morphism back to a single exact one. Such a reverse would need to
canonically select a weight
r\colon I\to\Theta
for each

(\Theta,f_{\theta})
, but the comonoid structure on
\Theta

provides no such section: the counit

!_{\Theta}\colon\Theta\to I
goes the wrong way — it discards
the parameter object rather than naming a point in it — and no
canonical
I\to\Theta
accompanies it. If such a canonical
section did exist it would name the trained model from the
architecture alone, making training unnecessary.
The tower therefore appears in this enriched setting as the
trivial-parameter slice of a richer categorical object
populated by the architectures that are actually trained;
the structural question an architecture poses to the tower is
the one categorical completeness below formalises — whether
the set of morphisms its weight space can realise lies in

\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
, and how much of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
it covers.

Once the tower and the parametric literature share a categorical
home, three structural questions about any published ML architecture
become precisely answerable, and none of them is answerable by
benchmark comparison alone.

Is the architecture’s equivariance a design choice or a
theorem?

Each level
\mathcal{L}_{k}
carries a canonical symmetry group
G_{k}
—
species permutations at
\mathcal{L}_{0}
–
\mathcal{L}_{3}
, graph automorphisms at

\mathcal{L}_{4}
, the permutation-inversion group at
\mathcal{L}_{4.5}
, rigid
motions composed with graph automorphisms
SE(3)\ltimes\mathrm{Aut}(G)

at
\mathcal{L}_{5}
, gauge transformations on the electronic bundle
at
\mathcal{L}_{6}
, particle exchange at
\mathcal{L}_{7}
.
Membership in
\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
is defined by requiring strict

G_{k}
-equivariance of the underlying map at every parameter setting.
MACE’s Clebsch–Gordan tensor contractions enforce the
\mathcal{L}_{5}

symmetry
SE(3)\ltimes\mathrm{Aut}(G)
for all
\theta
, not just the
trained one;
membership at
\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}
is therefore a theorem about the MACE
architecture, not a fortunate property of training.
An architecture whose symmetry is merely learned through data
augmentation fails the membership condition and is not, in structural
terms, a parametric morphism at that level.

What can the architecture represent, independent of its
training data?

An architecture
(\Theta,f_{\theta})
is
categorically
complete
at level
k
on a morphism
\varphi
of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
if
some parameter setting
r\colon I\to\Theta
instantiates

f_{\theta}
to
\varphi
exactly — equivalently, if
\varphi

lies in the architecture’s
function class

\mathsf{Func}(\Theta,f_{\theta})\subseteq\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)(X,Y)
,
the set of instantiations as
r
ranges over

\mathcal{C}(I,\Theta)
(Remark
11.4
).
Completeness is a property of the function class, not of the
loss or the training set.
An architecture incomplete at level
k
will fail on every task
requiring a target morphism
\varphi
absent from

\mathsf{Func}(\Theta,f_{\theta})
, regardless of training-set
size, because no choice of weights realises
\varphi
.

Which tower-coherence conditions does the architecture
enforce?

The tower’s forgetful functors
U_{k}\colon\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)\to\mathcal{L}_{k-1}(P)

connect adjacent levels;
a model claiming content at multiple levels must respect the
relations
U_{k}
imposes on joint content.
Three such conditions are unenforced across the published literature.
The Eyring TST condition couples a learned rate law to the activation
barrier of the same model’s potential energy surface
(
\mathcal{L}_{3}\leftrightarrow\mathcal{L}_{5}
).
The categorical Wegscheider condition couples forward and reverse
rate constants through the thermodynamic
\Delta G^{\circ}

(
\mathcal{L}_{2}\leftrightarrow\mathcal{L}_{3}
).
The topological output-type condition demands a Hilbert-bundle-valued
output rather than a scalar energy to carry the Berry-phase invariant

[\gamma_{B}]\in H^{1}({C_{e}}(G)\setminus\mathcal{X}_{01},\mathbb{Z}_{2})
near conical
intersections (
\mathcal{L}_{5}\to\mathcal{L}_{6}
).
The first two are literature-wide architectural absences that new
designs could close;
the third is a theorem about output type — no reparametrisation of
a scalar-energy architecture yields a Berry connection, regardless of
training, body order, or receptive field.

These three questions are the analytical spine of the chapter.
They organise what the tower, read through the Para enrichment,
reveals about ML molecular modelling:
a precise structural classification of every major architecture,
a completeness diagnostic that is architectural rather than
empirical,
and a catalogue of tower-coherence conditions the current literature
does not enforce.

Vocabulary for the computational chemist and physicist

The categorical language below is unfamiliar outside category theory,
but each object has a direct operational reading.
The rest of the chapter can be read with this dictionary alone.

Parametric morphism
(\Theta,f_{\theta})
.

A neural network.

\Theta
is the parameter space (the set of possible weight values);

f_{\theta}
is the forward map from input structure to output
prediction.
Training selects a point
\theta^{*}\in\Theta
.

Reparametrisation
r\colon\Theta^{\prime}\to\Theta
.

A map relating two parameter spaces.
Operationally: weight tying (one shared weight used in multiple
places, realised by the copy map

\Delta\colon\Theta\to\Theta\otimes\Theta
), fine-tuning, or
transfer learning.

Counit
!_{\Theta}\colon\Theta\to I
.

The unique map from the parameter space to the monoidal unit,
paired with
\Delta_{\Theta}
to give
\Theta
its comonoid
structure. Operationally, the categorical bookkeeping that
“a parameter object can be formally discarded” — the
counterpart to the comultiplication’s “a parameter can be
copied”. It does
not
correspond to setting weights to
zero or any other ablated value; that operation, if needed,
requires a section
z_{\Theta}\colon I\to\Theta
going the
other way, which is extra data the comonoid alone does not
provide. The tower’s exact laws enter the parametric row
through the trivial-parameter embedding
\gamma_{k}
(which uses

\Theta=I
, the monoidal unit), not through
!_{\Theta}
.

Comultiplication

\Delta_{\Theta}\colon\Theta\to\Theta\otimes\Theta
.

Weight sharing.
In MACE, one learnable radial MLP
R_{nl}
and one shared element
embedding
h_{j}
enter every message-passing layer;

\Delta_{\Theta}
is the categorical record of that sharing.

Symmetry monad
M_{k}
.

The level-
k
symmetry group
G_{k}
packaged as an operation on the
category
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
.
A morphism of
M_{k}
-algebras is exactly a
G_{k}
-equivariant map.

\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
membership.

The architecture’s map is
G_{k}
-equivariant
by construction
,
for every parameter setting, not merely by training regularisation or
data augmentation.

Categorical completeness at level
k
.

The architecture’s function class contains the target morphism
of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
:
some parameter setting realises it exactly.
Independent of training data.

With this dictionary the downstream content reads operationally.
“MACE lives in
\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}
” means
Clebsch–Gordan
contractions enforce
SE(3)\ltimes\mathrm{Aut}(G)
equivariance at every
layer, for every
\theta
.
“MACE is not complete at
\mathcal{L}_{6}
” means
the output type is
scalar energy, which contains no Berry connection no matter how

\Theta
is parametrised
.
“Thermodynamic consistency at
\mathcal{L}_{2}
requires a comultiplication
on
\Theta
coupling forward and reverse rates” means
no
published kinetic network has the right weight-sharing structure to
guarantee detailed balance
.

Vocabulary for the mathematician

2-category.

Objects, 1-morphisms between objects, and 2-morphisms between
parallel 1-morphisms.
The canonical example is
\mathbf{Cat}
: categories, functors,
natural transformations.

Self-action convention.

The Para construction of
[
112
]
is defined for an

\mathcal{M}
-actegory
(\mathcal{C},\triangleright)
;
throughout this chapter we specialise to the self-action case

\mathcal{M}=\mathcal{C}
,
\triangleright=\otimes
with

(\mathcal{C},\otimes,I)
symmetric monoidal.
This is sufficient for every tower level considered.

\mathrm{Para}(\mathcal{C})
.

Same objects as
\mathcal{C}
;
1-morphisms
X\to Y
are pairs
(\Theta,f_{\theta})
with

f_{\theta}\colon\Theta\otimes X\to Y
in
\mathcal{C}
;
2-morphisms
(\Theta,f_{\theta})\Rightarrow(\Theta^{\prime},f_{\theta^{\prime}})

are reparametrisations
r\colon\Theta^{\prime}\to\Theta
satisfying

f_{\theta}\circ(r\otimes\mathrm{id}_{X})=f_{\theta^{\prime}}
.
Sequential composition tensors parameter spaces.

Monad and algebra.

A monad
(M,\eta,\mu)
on
\mathcal{C}
is an endofunctor with unit

\eta\colon\mathrm{id}\Rightarrow M
and multiplication

\mu\colon M\circ M\Rightarrow M
satisfying standard coherence.
The group-action monad
(G\times-,\,\eta,\,\mu)
on

\mathbf{Set}
has
M
-algebras exactly
G
-actions and
M
-algebra
homomorphisms exactly
G
-equivariant maps.
Equivariance, in this language, is membership in a category of

M
-algebras.

Lax algebra, and what we use of it.

Lax algebras for a 2-monad replace strict commutativity on the
algebra diagrams with explicit 2-cells.
We use this structure in one place only: a lax algebra over

\mathrm{Para}(T)
endows its parameter object
\Theta
with a

comonoid
structure (counit

!_{\Theta}\colon\Theta\to I
, comultiplication

\Delta_{\Theta}\colon\Theta\to\Theta\otimes\Theta
),
realising the parameter-discard and weight-sharing operations
of the chembox above.
This result is due to Gavranović et al.
[
112
]
.

Strict equivariance specialisation.

We work throughout with the specialisation in which the 1-morphism
equivariance square commutes
strictly
(the 2-cell on that
square is the identity);
only the parameter-space comonoid structure remains lax.
This matches how current ML molecular architectures enforce
equivariance, and is a proper sub-framework of the full lax-algebra
apparatus of
[
112
]
that loses no content we
need.

A reader prepared to take the Para 2-category and its parameter-space
comonoid as black boxes can proceed from the chembox translation
alone;
the formal apparatus of Section
11.1
is there to make
the translations precise, not to add a separate layer of content.

Chapter roadmap.

Section
11.1
defines
\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
via the
membership conditions (E
k
) and (C
k
), constructs the
trivial-parameter embedding
\gamma_{k}
, and states categorical
completeness as a property of the architecture’s function class.
Section
11.2
casts four existing categorical
frameworks for ML molecular modelling —
Natural Graph Networks
[
128
]
,
Baez–Pollard open reaction networks
[
28
]
,
Fritz Markov categories
[
104
]
,
and Bonchi et al. string diagrams
[
45
]
—
in tower language, identifying which membership condition
(E_{k})

each characterises.
Section
11.3
classifies the major ML
molecular architectures by the highest tower level they inhabit.
Sections
11.4
,
11.5
,
and
11.6
work through MACE, So3krates/SO3LR, and
QIM as the primary worked examples of
\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}
and the

\mathcal{L}_{5}
–
\mathcal{L}_{6}
boundary.
Section
11.7
states and proves the three
tower-incompleteness results: the Eyring TST coherence gap, the
Wegscheider consistency gap, and the topological output-type gap.
Section
11.8
synthesises these as a design
specification for the next generation of ML molecular architectures.

§11.1. The Para enrichment: formal construction

The chapter opener presented, informally, the Para 2-category

\mathrm{Para}(\mathcal{C})
, the Para enrichment
\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
at each
tower level, the trivial-parameter embedding
\gamma_{k}
, and
categorical completeness.
Those informal presentations set up the chapter’s principal results
but cannot state them:
MACE/NequIP completeness on smooth BO potentials at
\mathcal{L}_{5}
,
framed as a conditional under universal-approximation
hypotheses (Section
11.4
), and their structural
incompleteness on the Berry class
[\gamma_{B}]
at
\mathcal{L}_{6}

(Section
11.7
) are mathematical
assertions that demand precise definitions of function class
and of membership in
\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
.
This section supplies those definitions and motivates each choice as
it is made.

The tower construction of Chapters
2
–
10

supplies four families of data used here without redefinition:
the tower categories
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
;
the tower forgetful functors

U_{k}\colon\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)\to\mathcal{L}_{k-1}(P)
;
the exact tower constructions
F_{\!H},F_{\!G}^{T},\FP,F_{\!V},F_{\!6}
;
and at each level the canonical symmetry monad
M_{k}
with underlying
group
G_{k}
, recorded formally in the Tower-symmetries paragraph
below.
The copy–delete comonoid structure of the Markov categories of
Chapter
5
is, in (C
k
) below, the prototype for the
parameter-space comonoid.

Short reading path

If you are reading this section for operational content, three items
carry the load: Definition
11.2
(what membership in

\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
means at tower level
k
), the function-class
notion in Remark
11.4
(what an architecture

can
represent across its weight space), and
Definition
11.5
(whether a specific target morphism
lies in that function class).
The surrounding monoidal setup, the
\gamma_{k}
construction, and the
well-definedness proofs are the mathematical scaffolding that makes
those three items precise.

Monoidal setup.

Throughout,

(\mathcal{C},\otimes,I,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)
denotes a symmetric
monoidal category with:
monoidal product
\otimes
; unit object
I
;
associator

\alpha_{A,B,C}\colon(A\otimes B)\otimes C\xrightarrow{\sim}A\otimes(B\otimes C)
;
left unitor
\lambda_{A}\colon I\otimes A\xrightarrow{\sim}A
; and
right unitor
\rho_{A}\colon A\otimes I\xrightarrow{\sim}A
.

\mathcal{C}
contains each tower category
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
as a symmetric
monoidal sub-category;
the inclusion
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)\hookrightarrow\mathcal{C}
is faithful but
generally
not
full, since a morphism of
\mathcal{C}
between
two objects of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
is a morphism of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
only when it
respects the level-
k
structure constructed in the corresponding
tower chapter.
Accordingly
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)(X,Y)\subseteq\mathcal{C}(X,Y)
is a proper
sub-hom-set in general.

\mathcal{C}
also contains the parameter spaces of ML architectures
(defined just below) as additional objects not in any
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
.

Parameter spaces and generalised elements.

A
parameter space
throughout this section is an object

\Theta
of
\mathcal{C}
.
The parameter spaces that arise in ML architectures are vector spaces
(real-valued weights), smooth manifolds (neural-network weight
manifolds), or discrete sets (integer-valued hyperparameters) —
none of which are objects of any tower category
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
.
The tensor product
\Theta\otimes X
of such a parameter space with
a chemistry object
X\in\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
is likewise an object of

\mathcal{C}
but not of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
.
One parameter space is distinguished: the monoidal unit
\Theta=I

lies in
\mathcal{C}
and in every
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
, and serves as the
trivial-parameter case of Proposition
11.3
.

A
weight setting
on
\Theta
is formalised as a morphism

r\colon I\to\Theta
in
\mathcal{C}
— the categorical form of
“a point of
\Theta
.”
In
\mathcal{C}=\mathbf{Set}
,
r
corresponds to a literal element
of
\Theta
;
in a category of real or complex vector spaces, to a single vector
in
\Theta
(equivalently, a linear map
\mathbb{R}\to\Theta
or

\mathbb{C}\to\Theta
);
in general, to a
generalised element
in the sense of
categorical logic.
We write
r\colon I\to\Theta
rather than
\theta\in\Theta
to
keep the formalism category-theoretic;
the reader may freely translate.

The comonoid data of (C
k
) below — its counit

!_{\Theta}\colon\Theta\to I
and comultiplication

\Delta_{\Theta}\colon\Theta\to\Theta\otimes\Theta
— is a
comonoid
in
\mathcal{C}
, not in
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
: parameter
discard and weight sharing are comonoid operations on parameter
spaces, carried out in the ambient monoidal category.
Since the intermediate object
\Theta\otimes X
on which a
forward map
f_{\theta}
is defined lies outside
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)

whenever
\Theta\neq I
, the level-
k
condition (E
k
) below
is a genuine closure requirement on the set of morphisms an
architecture can realise across its weight space; this closure
is what makes
\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
a level-
k
-respecting
sub-structure of
\mathrm{Para}(\mathcal{C})
.

Tower symmetries and the meaning of
“morphism of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
”.

At each tower level

k\in\{0,1,2,3,4,4.5,5,6,7\}
, the tower construction of

\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
in the corresponding chapter equips it with the canonical
symmetry monad
M_{k}
and underlying group
G_{k}
tabulated in
Table
6
:
a morphism of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
is exactly an
M_{k}
-algebra homomorphism,
equivalently a
G_{k}
-equivariant map that respects any additional
structure
M_{k}
carries at that level — the

\dagger
-involution at
\mathcal{L}_{2}
, the gauge action on the electronic
Hilbert bundle
{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(N)}\to{C_{e}}(G)
at
\mathcal{L}_{6}
, the

\varepsilon
-deformation that accompanies the continuous field

\{A_{\varepsilon}^{G}\}
at
\mathcal{L}_{7}
.
The pair
(M_{k},G_{k})
is canonical, determined by the tower
construction up to isomorphism, and used throughout this section
without re-proof.
The phrase “morphism of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
” throughout this section
denotes an
M_{k}
-algebra homomorphism of this kind —
equivalently, an element of the sub-hom-set

\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)(X,Y)\subseteq\mathcal{C}(X,Y)
.

Compatibility of the tower embedding.

The trivial-parameter embedding
\gamma_{k}
of
Section
11.1.3
(Proposition
11.3

below) imposes one closure requirement on the embedding

\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)\hookrightarrow\mathcal{C}
beyond the Tower-symmetries
characterisation just recorded:
for every
X\in\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
and every
r\in\mathcal{C}(I,I)
, the
endomorphism

\lambda_{X}\circ(r\otimes\mathrm{id}_{X})\circ\lambda_{X}^{-1}\colon X\to X

is a morphism of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
.
This requirement is vacuous when

\mathcal{C}(I,I)=\{\mathrm{id}_{I}\}
(the case whenever the
monoidal unit
I
is terminal in
\mathcal{C}
, e.g. for

\mathcal{C}=\mathbf{Set}
),
and is a structural property of the tower’s construction when

\mathcal{C}(I,I)
is richer — for instance, the real or complex
scalars at tower levels where
\mathcal{C}
is enriched over
\mathbb{R}
or

\mathbb{C}
.

11.1.1. The Para 2-category

The Para 2-category is a formal device that treats an entire
parametric family
\{f_{\theta}\colon X\to Y\}_{\theta\in\Theta}

as a single 1-morphism
(\Theta,f_{\theta})
, distinct from any
particular trained instance.
This is what lets us speak about what functions an architecture

can
represent across its whole weight space, independently of
any one training run.

Definition 11.1

(
\mathrm{Para}(\mathcal{C})

[
112
]
)
.

The
Para 2-category

\mathrm{Para}(\mathcal{C})
has:

•

Objects:
the objects of
\mathcal{C}
.

•

1-morphisms
X\to Y
:
pairs
(\Theta,f_{\theta})

with
\Theta
an object of
\mathcal{C}
(the
parameter
space
) and
f_{\theta}\colon\Theta\otimes X\to Y
a morphism
of
\mathcal{C}
.

•

2-morphisms

(\Theta,f_{\theta})\Rightarrow(\Theta^{\prime},f_{\theta^{\prime}})
:

morphisms
r\colon\Theta^{\prime}\to\Theta
in
\mathcal{C}

(
reparametrisations
) satisfying

f_{\theta}\circ(r\otimes\mathrm{id}_{X})=f_{\theta^{\prime}}
.

•

Composition
of

(\Theta,f_{\theta})\colon X\to Y
and

(Q,g_{\phi})\colon Y\to Z
:

(Q,g_{\phi})\circ(\Theta,f_{\theta})\;:=\;\bigl(Q\otimes\Theta,\;g_{\phi}\circ(\mathrm{id}_{Q}\otimes f_{\theta})\circ\alpha_{Q,\Theta,X}\bigr),

where the associator
\alpha_{Q,\Theta,X}
re-brackets

(Q\otimes\Theta)\otimes X
as
Q\otimes(\Theta\otimes X)
so that
\mathrm{id}_{Q}\otimes f_{\theta}
applies.

•

Identity on
X
:

(I,\lambda_{X})
.

In the strict monoidal case (
\alpha,\lambda,\rho
all identities),
composition reduces to

g_{\phi}\circ(\mathrm{id}_{Q}\otimes f_{\theta})
and the identity on

X
to
(I,\mathrm{id}_{X})
.

11.1.2. The Para enrichment
\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)

6
records
(M_{k},G_{k})
and the
content of “morphism of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
” at each tower level.

M_{k}
at each tower level (column 2)
and the content of “morphism of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
” that
condition (

) requires every instantiation of

(\Theta,f_{\theta})
to satisfy (column 3).
The reference at the end of each row names the chapter where that
content was constructed.
ML architecture assignments appear in
Table

.

)

S_{N}\times S_{M}

of deformation
parameters (Chapter

)

An architecture is said to live at tower level
k
when two things
are true of it simultaneously:
at every admissible weight setting the map it produces respects the
level-
k
structure of Table
6
, and its weight
space itself records — as part of its design — the comonoid
structure of (C
k
) below: how a weight may be shared across
layers (comultiplication
\Delta_{\Theta}
) and the formal
discardability of the parameter object (counit
!_{\Theta}
).
These are different kinds of data:

•

(E
k
) is a condition on each trained instance, testable on
any one weight setting;

•

(C
k
) is a condition on the design of the parameter space,
fixed at design time and persisting across training runs.

A single underlying map
f_{\theta}
can be realised by architectures
with different comonoid disciplines — one sharing weights across
layers, another keeping them independent — and (C
k
) is what
distinguishes those architectures in
\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
.

Definition 11.2

(
\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
)
.

The
Para enrichment at tower level
k
is the sub-2-category

\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)\subset\mathrm{Para}(\mathcal{C})
with:

•

Objects:
the objects of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
.

•

1-morphisms
X\to Y
:
parametric morphisms

(\Theta,f_{\theta})
of
\mathrm{Para}(\mathcal{C})
with
X,Y\in\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
and
\Theta
a parameter space (setup above),
satisfying both conditions below.

•

2-morphisms:
reparametrisations of

\mathrm{Para}(\mathcal{C})
between such 1-morphisms.

(E
k
) Per-parameter level-
k

equivariance.

For every morphism
r\colon I\to\Theta
in
\mathcal{C}
, the

instantiation of
f_{\theta}
at
r
,

f_{\theta}\circ(r\otimes\mathrm{id}_{X})\circ\lambda_{X}^{-1}\;\colon\;X\to Y,

(32)

is a morphism of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
(Table
6
).
In the group-action case
M_{k}(X)=G_{k}\times X
, this is
equivalent to the pointwise statement

f_{\theta}(g\cdot x)=g\cdot f_{\theta}(x)
for every

\theta\in\Theta
,
g\in G_{k}
,
x\in X
, recovering the
chembox reading of the chapter opener.

(C
k
) Parameter-space comonoid.

\Theta
is equipped with

•

a counit
!_{\Theta}\colon\Theta\to I
in
\mathcal{C}

— the
parameter-discard
map (not a zero-weight
choice; see Remark
11.4
);

•

a comultiplication

\Delta_{\Theta}\colon\Theta\to\Theta\otimes\Theta
in

\mathcal{C}
— the
weight-sharing
map;

satisfying coassociativity and counitality.

Why (E
k
) is stated per-parameter.

Condition (
32
) is phrased per-parameter — one check per

r\colon I\to\Theta
— rather than as a single condition on the
pair
(\Theta,f_{\theta})
at the level of the ambient category

\mathrm{Para}(\mathcal{C})
.
Two reasons.
First, it is directly testable:
given an architecture at a particular trained weight setting
r^{*}
,
one verifies (
32
) by checking that the instantiation at

r^{*}
is a morphism of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
, with no further categorical
apparatus required.
Second, the per-parameter statement matches the chemist’s reading of
membership from the chapter chembox:
an architecture lives at level
k
exactly when every weight setting
it admits — not just the trained one — yields a level-
k

morphism.

Why a comonoid on
\Theta
, and why this
particular one.

The operations a parameter space admits — duplicate a weight
(for sharing across layers) and discard a weight (formally
forgetting the parameter object) — are exactly those of a
comonoid in a symmetric monoidal category.
This is not a structure newly imported from
[
112
]

for the present chapter:
Chapter
5
already uses the same
(\Delta,!)
data, there
as the copy–delete morphisms on every object of a Markov category,
where
\Delta
copies a random sample and
!
discards one.
Here the formal content is identical and the interpretation shifts:

\Delta
routes a single weight into two layers (rather than copying
a sample to two outputs);
!
records the parameter object as
formally discardable (the categorical counterpart of the
discardable sample, not a weight-zeroing or weight-ablation
operation).
We record (C
k
) explicitly because weight-sharing discipline is
architectural data:
two networks with the same underlying map
f_{\theta}
but different
comonoid structures on
\Theta
are different architectures, and

\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
must distinguish them.

11.1.3. The trivial-parameter embedding
\gamma_{k}

We want the Para enrichment to
extend
the exact tower, not
replace it: every exact morphism of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
should appear inside

\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
as the trivial-parameter special case
\Theta=I
.
With this in place, the monograph’s earlier theorems about

\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
apply verbatim to the
\Theta=I
slice, and the
parametric structure is built
on top of
the tower, not in
competition with it.

Proposition 11.3

(Trivial-parameter embedding)
.

The assignment

\gamma_{k}\colon\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)\;\longrightarrow\;\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P),\qquad\gamma_{k}(X)=X,\qquad\gamma_{k}\bigl(f\colon X\to Y\bigr)\;=\;\bigl(I,\;f\circ\lambda_{X}\bigr)

is a symmetric monoidal functor
(strong in the general monoidal case, strict when
\mathcal{C}
is
strict) that identifies
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
with the full sub-2-category of

\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
whose 1-morphisms have trivial parameter space

\Theta=I
.

Proof.

Well-definedness.

For
r\in\mathcal{C}(I,I)
, write

\psi(r):=\lambda_{X}\circ(r\otimes\mathrm{id}_{X})\circ\lambda_{X}^{-1}\colon X\to X

for the unit-whiskered endomorphism of
X
;
in particular
\psi(\mathrm{id}_{I})=\mathrm{id}_{X}
.
The instantiation of
(I,\,f\circ\lambda_{X})
at
r
equals

(f\circ\lambda_{X})\circ(r\otimes\mathrm{id}_{X})\circ\lambda_{X}^{-1}\;=\;f\circ\psi(r)\;\colon\;X\to Y.

By the compatibility requirement on the tower embedding stated in the
monoidal setup,
\psi(r)\in\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)(X,X)
for every

r\in\mathcal{C}(I,I)
;
composition with
f\in\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)(X,Y)
then yields

f\circ\psi(r)\in\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)(X,Y)
by closure of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
under
composition.
Condition (E
k
) therefore holds.
Condition (C
k
) holds with
I
carrying the terminal comonoid

(\mathrm{id}_{I},\;\lambda_{I}^{-1})
.

Functoriality.

\gamma_{k}(\mathrm{id}_{X})=(I,\lambda_{X})
is the identity 1-morphism
on
X
in
\mathrm{Para}(\mathcal{C})
.
Sequential composition in
\mathrm{Para}(\mathcal{C})
of
\gamma_{k}(f)
and

\gamma_{k}(g)
produces parameter space
I\otimes I
, which
corresponds to
I
via the canonical monoidal iso

\lambda_{I}\colon I\otimes I\xrightarrow{\sim}I
:
equality in the strict case, a canonical iso in general.

Identification of the image.

A 1-morphism
(I,h)
of
\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)(X,Y)
determines

h\circ\lambda_{X}^{-1}\in\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)(X,Y)

(a morphism of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
by (
32
));
this assignment is inverse to
\gamma_{k}
on trivial-parameter
hom-sets.
∎

Remark 11.4

(Function class; no reverse to
\gamma_{k}
)
.

The
function class
of a 1-morphism

(\Theta,f_{\theta})\in\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)(X,Y)
is the set of all
instantiations as
r
ranges over
\mathcal{C}(I,\Theta)
:

\mathsf{Func}(\Theta,f_{\theta})\;:=\;\bigl\{\,f_{\theta}\circ(r\otimes\mathrm{id}_{X})\circ\lambda_{X}^{-1}\;:\;r\in\mathcal{C}(I,\Theta)\,\bigr\}\;\subseteq\;\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)(X,Y).

Operationally,
\mathsf{Func}(\Theta,f_{\theta})
is the set of
morphisms the architecture
can
represent for some choice of
weights, as opposed to the specific one a training run happens to
pick.
Condition (
32
) is precisely the assertion

\mathsf{Func}(\Theta,f_{\theta})\subseteq\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)(X,Y)
: every
weight setting gives a level-
k
morphism.

There is no canonical 2-functor
\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)\to\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)

collapsing
(\Theta,f_{\theta})
to a single exact morphism:
the counit
!_{\Theta}\colon\Theta\to I
does not select a point of

\Theta
.
(If it did, training would be unnecessary: the counit would produce
the right model for free.)
Categorical completeness below is therefore stated as a property of
the function class, not as a condition on any reverse map to

\gamma_{k}
.

11.1.4. Categorical completeness

Membership in
\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
guarantees that every element of

\mathsf{Func}(\Theta,f_{\theta})
is a level-
k
morphism;
it does not say
which
level-
k
morphisms appear there.
The question categorical completeness asks is the second one:
given a specific target morphism
\varphi
of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
, is

\varphi
in the function class?

The targets of applied interest are those produced by the exact
tower constructions of earlier chapters.
At
\mathcal{L}_{1}
, the target is the enthalpy the Hess functor
F_{\!H}

assigns to a specific reaction.
At
\mathcal{L}_{3}
, it is the Markov kernel
\FP
assigns to a transition.
At
\mathcal{L}_{5}
, it is the Born–Oppenheimer potential
F_{\!V}
yields on a
specific molecular configuration.
At
\mathcal{L}_{6}
, it is the Hilbert bundle
F_{\!6}
produces on a
molecule, including the Berry class
[\gamma_{B}]
the bundle carries
at a conical intersection.
In each case
\varphi
is a specific morphism of the corresponding

\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
, identifiable in the chapter where the tower construction
was defined.

Definition 11.5

(Categorical completeness)
.

Let
(\Theta,f_{\theta})\in\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)(X,Y)
and let

\varphi\colon X\to Y
be a morphism of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
.
The parametric morphism
(\Theta,f_{\theta})
is

categorically complete on
\varphi
if

\varphi\in\mathsf{Func}(\Theta,f_{\theta})
:
there exists
r\colon I\to\Theta
in
\mathcal{C}
with

f_{\theta}\circ(r\otimes\mathrm{id}_{X})\circ\lambda_{X}^{-1}\;=\;\varphi\qquad\text{in }\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)(X,Y).

It is
complete on a class
\mathcal{S}\subseteq\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)(X,Y)
if complete on every
\varphi\in\mathcal{S}
, and

complete at level
k
if complete on every morphism of

\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)(X,Y)
.

Completeness is a property of the architecture — its parameter
space, its forward map, its closure under choice of weights — and
is logically independent of any training procedure.
No training recovers a target absent from the function class.

ML molecular architectures are typically complete on physically
meaningful subclasses.
At
\mathcal{L}_{5}
, for instance, MACE/NequIP completeness on a dense
subclass of smooth BO potentials is framed conditionally on
universal-approximation hypotheses in
Section
11.4
.
They are not complete on all of
\mathcal{L}_{5}(P)(X,Y)
, and at
\mathcal{L}_{6}

they are incomplete in a structurally topological way.
Section
11.7
identifies three specific

\varphi
— one at
\mathcal{L}_{6}
structurally outside the function
class of every scalar-energy architecture, and two at

\mathcal{L}_{2}
/
\mathcal{L}_{3}
outside the function classes of the published
kinetic and joint kinetic-energetic architectures — that are
the tower-coherence gaps the rest of the chapter
analyses.

Completeness is architectural, not empirical

Where does completeness bite?
At
\mathcal{L}_{6}
, Proposition
11.19
shows
that the Berry class

[\gamma_{B}]\in H^{1}({C_{e}}(G)\setminus\mathcal{X}_{01},\mathbb{Z}_{2})
carried by the
Hilbert bundle
F_{\!6}
at a conical intersection lies outside

\mathsf{Func}(\Theta,f_{\theta})
for
every

SE(3)
-equivariant scalar-energy force field.
The reason is type-theoretic:
[\gamma_{B}]
is not a pointwise
function on
{C_{e}}(G)
at all but a
\mathbb{Z}_{2}
-valued cohomology class
assigning a value to each homology class of loops in

{C_{e}}(G)\setminus\mathcal{X}_{01}
; a scalar-valued output, which is a
function on
{C_{e}}(G)
, cannot represent such a class.
No
r\colon I\to\Theta
in a scalar-output architecture produces
a map that carries
[\gamma_{B}]
.
The failure is an output-type obstruction at the architecture level,
revealed by the tower and not addressable by any training procedure.

§11.2. External categorical frameworks in tower language

The Para enrichment
\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
of
Section
11.1
unifies, into a single nested
hierarchy, characterisations of the membership condition
(E
k
) of Definition
11.2
that were developed
independently — before this monograph’s tower — one level
at a time.
In detail:
(E
0
) is Meseguer–Montanari’s free-strict-SMC morphism
condition
[
221
]
;
(E
3
)’s Markov-kernel core is, on the stochastic-kinetics
side, Fritz’s Markov-category morphism
condition
[
104
]
(positivity, probability
conservation), with species-permutation equivariance the
additional tower-specific component; and, on the
composable-networks side, Baez and Pollard’s gray-box
functor condition on open reaction
networks
[
28
]
;
(E
4
) is de Haan, Cohen, and Welling’s Natural Graph Networks
naturality on molecular graphs
[
128
]

and Bonchi et al.’s DPO-compatible string-diagram rewriting of
mechanistic
graphs
[
45
]
;
(E
5
) is Clebsch–Gordan-augmented NGN, as realised in
NequIP
[
37
]
, MACE
[
34
]
,
and So3krates
[
100
]
.
Each of these four external frameworks characterises one
tower level on its own terms and goes no further.
The Cruttwell–Gavranović framework of categorical
gradient-based learning
[
70
]
,
treated separately below, runs perpendicular to this
enumeration: it does not pair with a single tower level but
supplies the 2-categorical backdrop for gradient-based
training of any
\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
architecture
(Section
11.2.3
).
What the tower adds, via the forgetful functors

U_{k}\colon\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)\to\mathcal{L}_{k-1}(P)
of
Section
11.1
, is nesting:
the hierarchy
\mathcal{L}_{0}(P)\leftarrow\mathcal{L}_{1}(P)\leftarrow\cdots\leftarrow\mathcal{L}_{7}(P)
makes each (E
k
) strictly refine
(E
k-1
), so a model at level
k
inherits every lower-level
condition and can fail higher-level ones in locatable ways —
by naming the specific forgetful functor above which it falls.

For each of the four level-pairing frameworks, this section
records three things:
(a) the tower level
k
at which (E
k
) identifies with the
framework;
(b) a direct verification of the identification against the
hom-set characterisation

\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)(X,Y)\subseteq\mathcal{C}(X,Y)
of
Section
11.1
;
and (c) the forgetful functor above which the framework’s
categorical vocabulary runs out.
The CGGWZ subsection follows a different template, since the
framework has no (E
k
) to identify and no
U_{k}
above which
its vocabulary runs out — both of these facts being
consequences of its perpendicularity.
The resulting pairings feed every subsequent section of the
chapter:
Section
11.3
uses them as the
classification criterion (Table
7
);
Section
11.4
uses the
(E_{5})
lift to analyse
MACE and NequIP’s completeness quantitatively;
Section
11.5
uses the same
(E_{5})

condition, realised differently, to place So3krates’s

SE(3)
-equivariant self-attention;
Section
11.6
works through QIM as a
bidirectional
\mathcal{L}_{5}
-type worked example (non-strict

\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}
under its Coulomb-matrix representation) whose
approximation target references
\mathcal{L}_{6}
through the
Born–Oppenheimer ground-state section
\sigma_{0}
;
and Section
11.7
uses the joint
boundary identified here — the Berry class
[\gamma_{B}]

at
\mathcal{L}_{6}
that no external framework expresses — to state
the topological obstruction to scalar-energy force fields.

Reading paths through this section

A chemist reading for operational content will find, at the
start of each subsection, the condition membership in

\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
places on an architecture expressed in
chemistry terms (atom-relabelling invariance,
probability conservation, DPO-valid bond rearrangement,
encoder–decoder bidirectionality);
the surrounding categorical exposition can be skipped.

A physicist reading for the concrete membership condition at
each level will find it stated in each subsubsection’s
proposition or paragraph:
an explicit Wigner
D
-matrix equivariance

f_{\theta}(R\cdot\mathbf{R})=D(R)f_{\theta}(\mathbf{R})
for
(E
5
),
the graph-automorphism version
f_{\theta}(\sigma\cdot G)=D(\sigma)f_{\theta}(G)
for (E
4
),
Markov-kernel preservation (positivity, probability
conservation) together with species-permutation covariance of
the CME generator
\Omega
for (E
3
),
DPO-span equivariance on
\mathbf{LGraph}_{P}
for (E
4
) in its
mechanistic form,
and the Berry-class obstruction
[\gamma_{B}]
whose absence in
every framework’s vocabulary is the content of the mathboxes
below.

A mathematician reading for verification will find each
framework-tower pairing stated as a proposition or explicit
iff-condition reducing to Definition
11.2
;
each subsection closes with a mathbox titled
“Where [framework] stops in the tower” recording the
specific forgetful functor above which the external
framework’s vocabulary runs out.

11.2.1. De Haan–Cohen–Welling at
\mathcal{L}_{4}^{\mathrm{Para}}
:
graph naturality

Chemically:

membership in
\mathcal{L}_{4}^{\mathrm{Para}}
asks a force field to produce the
same output for any pair of molecular graphs related by atom
relabelling (same graph, same prediction regardless of how
atoms are numbered);
membership in
\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}
additionally asks the output to
transform correctly under physical rotations and translations
of the geometry.
The first condition is Natural Graph Networks naturality
(this subsection);
the second is NGN augmented by Clebsch–Gordan tensor products,
realised by NequIP, MACE, and So3krates.

The
Natural Graph Networks
(NGN) framework of de Haan,
Cohen, and Welling
[
128
]
gives the
categorical language for message-passing neural networks on
graphs.
Its central objects are
graph feature spaces
: functors

\rho\colon\mathbf{Graph}\to\mathbf{Vec}

from a groupoid of graphs (with graph isomorphisms as morphisms)
to vector spaces.
A
natural graph network layer
between two such feature
spaces is a natural transformation

K\colon\rho\Rightarrow\rho^{\prime}
,
a family of maps
K_{G}\colon\rho(G)\to\rho^{\prime}(G)
commuting
with every graph isomorphism.
Naturality is exactly equivariance under graph-level
symmetries — that is, under
\mathrm{Aut}(G)
.

Proposition 11.6

(NGN naturality is
(E_{4})
)
.

At tower level
k=4
, where
G_{4}=\mathrm{Aut}(G)
acts on the
labelled-graph category
\mathbf{LGraph}_{P}
of
Chapter
6
:

(i)

Graph feature spaces
\rho\colon\mathbf{Graph}\to\mathbf{Vec}
restricted to the objects of
\mathbf{LGraph}_{P}
are
exactly the
\mathrm{Aut}(G)
-equivariant feature maps at

\mathcal{L}_{4}(P)
.

(ii)

The NGN naturality condition of

[
128
]
is the membership
condition (
32
) at
k=4
:

f_{\theta}(\sigma\cdot G)\;=\;D(\sigma)\,f_{\theta}(G)\qquad\text{for all }\sigma\in\mathrm{Aut}(G),

where
D
is the representation of
\mathrm{Aut}(G)
on the
output feature channels.

(iii)

Local-to-global: an architecture satisfying naturality
at every message-passing edge satisfies it globally on the
molecular graph
[
128
]
.

Proof.

Claims (i) and (ii) are direct comparisons with
Definition
11.2
at
k=4
:
for any molecular graph
G\in\mathbf{LGraph}_{P}
, the automorphisms of

G
in
\mathbf{Graph}
are exactly the elements of
\mathrm{Aut}(G)
,
and naturality of a feature map
f_{\theta}
under these
automorphisms is by definition the
(E_{4})
condition.
Claim (iii) is the main result of
[
128
]
;
we import it without re-proof.
∎

Lifting NGN from
\mathcal{L}_{4}^{\mathrm{Para}}
to

\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}
.

NGN in its native form does not reach
\mathcal{L}_{5}
, whose symmetry
group
G_{5}=SE(3)\ltimes\mathrm{Aut}(G)
also acts by rotations and
translations on geometric positions in
\mathbb{R}^{3n}

(Chapter
8
).
An architecture built on NGN foundations lifts to
\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}

only when it augments graph-level naturality with

SE(3)
-equivariant operations on geometric features.
Three such lifts appear in current ML literature.
NequIP
[
37
]
and
MACE
[
34
]
combine NGN naturality with
Clebsch–Gordan tensor products of irreducible
SE(3)

representations on edge features, enforcing the full

(E_{5})
-condition

f_{\theta}(R\cdot\mathbf{R})\;=\;D(R)\,f_{\theta}(\mathbf{R})\qquad\text{for all }R\in SE(3)\ltimes\mathrm{Aut}(G),

where
D(R)
is the block-diagonal Wigner
D
-matrix on the
output irrep channels.
So3krates
[
100
]
enforces the same

(E_{5})
-condition directly via
SE(3)
-equivariant
self-attention (Section
11.5
).
Distance-invariant message passing (as in SchNet) trades

SE(3)
-equivariance for
SE(3)
-invariance, producing a scalar
output and so landing in
\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}
with a function class
restricted to
SE(3)
-invariant scalars.

A force field satisfying the
(E_{5})
-form above predicts the
same energy on any pair of
SE(3)\ltimes\mathrm{Aut}(G)
-equivalent
geometries — translations, rotations, and permutations of
identical atoms give identical outputs.
The additional reflection invariance that ML force fields
typically also enforce (yielding full
E(3)
-equivariance in
the ML sense) lives one level further: it is
\mathcal{L}_{4.5}^{\mathrm{Para}}

content, supplied by the parity factor

\mathbb{Z}_{2}^{k}\subset G^{*}
(Chapter
7
).

Where NGN stops in the tower

The category
\mathbf{Graph}
of
[
128
]

carries nodes and edge features but nothing above.
Natively NGN captures
\mathcal{L}_{4}^{\mathrm{Para}}
’s
\mathrm{Aut}(G)
-symmetry;
augmented with
SE(3)
-equivariant operations (NequIP, MACE,
So3krates) it reaches
\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}
.
Above
\mathcal{L}_{5}
it runs out of content:
the forgetful functor

U_{6}\colon\mathcal{L}_{6}(P)\to\mathcal{L}_{5}(P)

discards the Hilbert bundle
{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(N)}\to{C_{e}}(G)
, the Berry
connection
A_{mn}^{\mu}
, and the topological phase

[\gamma_{B}]\in H^{1}({C_{e}}(G)\setminus\mathcal{X}_{01},\mathbb{Z}_{2})
;
none of these has a counterpart in
\mathbf{Graph}
, augmented
or not.
On the other side of the tower, the thermodynamic functor

F_{\!G}^{T}\colon\mathcal{L}_{2}(P)\to B\mathbb{R}
is similarly absent:
NGN has no slot for enthalpy, entropy, or the Wegscheider
kernel
\ker F_{\!G}^{T}
.
NGN, with or without
SE(3)
-augmentation, therefore
characterises
\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
at most for
k\leq 5
;
it is silent on
\mathcal{L}_{6}^{\mathrm{Para}}
and on the thermodynamic content
of
\mathcal{L}_{k}
for
k\leq 3
.

11.2.2. Combinatorial tower levels
\mathcal{L}_{0}
,
\mathcal{L}_{3}
,

\mathcal{L}_{4}
: Meseguer–Montanari, Baez–Pollard, Fritz, Bonchi et
al.

Chemically:

membership in
\mathcal{L}_{0}^{\mathrm{Para}}
asks a yield or outcome predictor
to respect stoichiometric balance and atom-permutation
symmetry;
membership in
\mathcal{L}_{3}^{\mathrm{Para}}
asks a kinetic or rate predictor to
preserve positivity of concentrations, conservation of
probability, and species-permutation symmetry of the CME
generator;
membership in
\mathcal{L}_{4}^{\mathrm{Para}}
asks a mechanism or retrosynthesis
predictor to produce bond rearrangements realisable as DPO
pushout complements in the labelled molecular graph.

At the combinatorial tower levels
\mathcal{L}_{0}
,
\mathcal{L}_{3}
,
\mathcal{L}_{4}
—
stoichiometry, kinetics, and bond-topological mechanisms —
the membership conditions (E
0
), (E
3
), (E
4
) each admit
an explicit external characterisation.
Four categorical frameworks supply these characterisations in a
form that an architecture can verify or fail, and together they
give the section’s classification criterion for the three lowest
non-trivial Para levels.

Stoichiometry at
\mathcal{L}_{0}^{\mathrm{Para}}
, open kinetics at

\mathcal{L}_{3}^{\mathrm{Para}}
: Meseguer–Montanari and Baez–Pollard.

The stoichiometric tower category
\mathcal{L}_{0}(P)
is exactly the
free strict SMC on a Petri net
P
of Meseguer and
Montanari
[
221
]

(Chapter
2
).
Baez and Pollard
[
28
]
extend this
construction to
open
reaction networks, producing a
gray-box functor at
\mathcal{L}_{3}
that reads off the input–output
kinetics of a composed network from its boundary data
(Theorem
5.30
).
A closely related taxonomy of net categories — commutative
monoidal category nets,
\Sigma
-nets, and further variants —
is developed by Baez, Genovese, Master, and
Shulman
[
26
]
;

\mathcal{L}_{0}(P)
of the tower corresponds to one vertex of that
taxonomy (the free strict SMC), with Baez–Master’s
CMC
[
27
]
a quotient in which all symmetry
morphisms are identified
(Remark
2.17
).

The Para content of these identifications is direct.
A yield or reaction-outcome predictor
(\Theta,f_{\theta})

lies in
\mathcal{L}_{0}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
iff its function class

\mathsf{Func}(\Theta,f_{\theta})

(Remark
11.4
) consists of

\mathrm{Sym}(\mathcal{S})
-equivariant maps with outputs in
\mathbb{N}^{|\mathcal{S}|}

(or a real-valued approximation thereof).
A composed reaction-network predictor lies in the open-network
analogue of
\mathcal{L}_{3}^{\mathrm{Para}}
iff its interface kinetics compose by
pushout as in
[
28
]
.
Retrosynthesis planners and mechanistic networks in current
use, however, treat reactions as isolated events rather than
as morphisms composable by pushout;
the bicategory
\mathrm{Csp}(\mathcal{L}_{4}^{\mathrm{Para}})
of open mechanistic
networks thus remains an open target for the tower programme.

Stochastic kinetics at
\mathcal{L}_{3}^{\mathrm{Para}}
: Fritz Markov
categories.

Fritz’s synthetic framework of Markov
categories
[
104
]
supplies the Markov-kernel
component of (E
3
) in directly verifiable form: preservation
of positivity and conservation of probability. The full
(E
3
) of the tower combines this Markov-kernel structure
with species-permutation equivariance of the CME generator,
the second component being tower-specific content not in
Fritz’s bare framework.
The category
\Stoch
of Markov kernels is the canonical
Markov category; the kinetic functor

\FP\colon\mathcal{L}_{0}(P)\to\Stoch
of
Section
5.2
, which assembles the CME generator

\Omega=\sum_{r}\FP(r)
, is a morphism of Markov categories
in the single-state-space sense of
Remark
5.3
.
A neural kinetic model
(\Theta,f_{\theta})
lies in

\mathcal{L}_{3}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
iff every instantiation

f_{\theta}\circ(r\otimes\mathrm{id}_{X})\circ\lambda_{X}^{-1}

satisfies both components of (E
3
): it is a morphism of
Markov categories in Fritz’s sense
(preserving positivity of concentrations and conservation of
probability), and it intertwines rate-preserving species
permutations with the generator
\Omega

(Proposition
5.15
).

\mathcal{L}_{3}^{\mathrm{Para}}
-membership does not, however, imply

\mathcal{L}_{2}^{\mathrm{Para}}
-membership:
Markov-category morphism status is about probability and
kinetics, while
\dagger
-compatibility at
\mathcal{L}_{2}
is forced
by the thermodynamic structure and the categorical Wegscheider
condition
\ker F_{\!G}^{T}
.
The forgetful functor
U_{3}\colon\mathcal{L}_{3}(P)\to\mathcal{L}_{2}(P)
is
therefore where the Markov-category vocabulary of

[
104
]
first leaves a gap that a neural
kinetic model must fill separately — and the gap that
Section
11.3
documents for current
neural kinetic models in its thermodynamic column.

Mechanisms at
\mathcal{L}_{4}^{\mathrm{Para}}
: Bonchi et al. string
diagrams.

Part II of Bonchi, Gadducci, Kissinger, Sobociński, and
Zanasi’s
String Diagram Rewrite
Theory

[
45
]
establishes that DPO
rewriting of hypergraphs modulo symmetric monoidal category
equations corresponds to string-diagram rewriting in a free
SMC.
This is the categorical foundation on which the tower’s

\mathcal{L}_{4}(P)
is built (Chapter
6
):
the six DPO generators of Definition
6.18
—
heterolytic and homolytic cleavage, electron-pair migration,
and their reverses — are the string-diagram generators of
the free SMC that controls bond rearrangements, and DPO
rewriting in the labelled-graph category
\mathbf{LGraph}_{P}
is the
operational semantics for their composition.

An ML model
(\Theta,f_{\theta})
for retrosynthesis or
mechanism prediction lies in
\mathcal{L}_{4}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
iff its function
class
\mathsf{Func}(\Theta,f_{\theta})
consists of

\mathrm{Aut}(G)
-equivariant DPO-span morphisms that preserve bond
order, formal charges, and lone pairs.
Molecular Transformer
[
266
]
and
similar sequence-to-sequence models implicitly approximate
morphisms in this string-diagram category by learning
reaction-template patterns, but without the formal DPO
constraint that would guarantee predicted bond changes remain
geometrically realisable in
\mathbf{LGraph}_{P}
.

Where the combinatorial frameworks stop

Fritz’s Markov categories
[
104
]
characterise
the Markov-kernel component of
\mathcal{L}_{3}^{\mathrm{Para}}
;
Bonchi et al.’s string-diagram
rewriting
[
45
]
characterises the
DPO-rewriting component of
\mathcal{L}_{4}^{\mathrm{Para}}
;
Meseguer–Montanari
[
221
]
and
Baez–Pollard
[
28
]
characterise
\mathcal{L}_{0}
and
open-
\mathcal{L}_{3}
respectively.
Each framework supplies the structural component that
distinguishes its tower level from the next lower one;
species-permutation equivariance at
\mathcal{L}_{3}
and

\mathrm{Aut}(G)
-equivariance at
\mathcal{L}_{4}
are tower-specific
additions layered on top of these structural components.
None of the four reaches thermodynamics:
the forgetful functor
U_{2}\colon\mathcal{L}_{2}(P)\to\mathcal{L}_{1}(P)

preserves enthalpy and the dagger structure, and
(E_{2})
—

\dagger
-equivariance and preservation of
\ker F_{\!G}^{T}
—
is not expressible in any of these frameworks.
The tower’s cokernel forcing of
\mathcal{L}_{1}\to\mathcal{L}_{2}
is precisely
the statement that Fritz’s vocabulary does not suffice.
Geometry and electronic structure are also out of reach:
none of the four frameworks carries a slot for

{C_{e}}(G)=\mathbb{R}^{3n}/G_{5}
or for the Hilbert bundle

{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(N)}\to{C_{e}}(G)
of
\mathcal{L}_{6}
.

11.2.3. The Cruttwell–Gavranović framework and the

\mathcal{L}_{5}
–
\mathcal{L}_{6}
interface

Chemically:

bidirectional encoder–decoder–property architectures at the

\mathcal{L}_{5}
–
\mathcal{L}_{6}
interface, of which QIM
[
89
]

is the primary published example
(Section
11.6
), run in two directions through
a shared latent space:
geometry
\to
latent
\to
property prediction, and
geometry
\to
latent
\to
reconstructed geometry.
Each constituent forward map sits at
\mathcal{L}_{5}
-type — strict

\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
when the representation is fully equivariant,
non-strict for QIM under its Coulomb-matrix representation
(Section
11.6
) — and the architecture as a
whole is a
triple
of such maps trained jointly.
The reconstruction and property errors (RMSD, MAE) are
measurable scalar quantities produced by training, not
categorical data attached to the morphisms.

The categorical framework supplied for gradient-trained
parametric architectures by Cruttwell, Gavranović, Ghani,
Wilson, and Zanasi
[
70
]
differs
structurally from the three preceding bridges.
Markov categories characterise the Markov-kernel component of
(E
3
); string diagrams characterise the DPO-rewriting
component of (E
4
); NGN, natively or augmented with

SE(3)
-equivariant operations, characterises the equivariance
components of (E
4
) and (E
5
).
Each identifies a specific tower level.
The CGGWZ framework does not.
Its subject is the compositional semantics of gradient-based
learning in the 2-category
\mathrm{Para}(\mathcal{C})
:
a
parametric lens
is a forward–backward pair of
morphisms, with forward component

f\colon\Theta\otimes X\to Y
in
\mathrm{Para}(\mathcal{C})
and
a backward component propagating changes in outputs to changes
in inputs and parameters, so that sequential composition of
lenses realises the chain rule compositionally.
The framework is about how gradient descent composes, not about
what a trained model represents at a particular tower level.

CGGWZ runs perpendicular to the tower.

Every
\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
1-morphism trained by backpropagation
admits the CGGWZ lens structure once its gradient data is made
explicit — a kinetic model at
\mathcal{L}_{3}^{\mathrm{Para}}
just as much as a
force field at
\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}
or a mechanism predictor at

\mathcal{L}_{4}^{\mathrm{Para}}
.
Lens status is therefore orthogonal to (E
k
):
it does not distinguish tower levels, and no forgetful functor

U_{k}\colon\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)\to\mathcal{L}_{k-1}(P)
measures where the
framework’s vocabulary runs out, because its vocabulary tracks
gradient flow rather than level-specific structure.
The CGGWZ framework is consequently not a bridge to a single

\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
in the sense of the three preceding
subsections.

What CGGWZ
does
supply to the tower programme is
structural backdrop for Section
11.1
rather than
level-specific characterisation:
the 2-category
\mathrm{Para}(\mathcal{C})
itself
(Definition
11.1
);
the comonoid structure on parameter spaces in
condition (C
k
) of Definition
11.2
— counit

!_{\Theta}\colon\Theta\to I
and comultiplication

\Delta_{\Theta}\colon\Theta\to\Theta\otimes\Theta
—
derived in Theorem G.10 of
[
112
]
as the
lax-algebra coherence data of a
\mathrm{Para}(T)
-algebra;
and the weight-tying semantics
(
\Delta_{\Theta}
routes one weight to two layers) and
parameter-discard semantics (
!_{\Theta}
as the categorical
record that
\Theta
can be formally discarded, not as a
zero-weight choice) on which (C
k
) rests.
These contributions are to the background of every

\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
, not to the classification of any particular
architecture at a particular level.

The encoder–decoder triple at the

\mathcal{L}_{5}
–
\mathcal{L}_{6}
interface, in correct categorical language.

A common informal reading takes QIM’s encoder–decoder
structure to be a parametric lens.
The categorical facts do not support this.
QIM is three parametric maps of
\mathcal{L}_{5}
-type through
a shared latent
Z
(Section
11.6
;
non-strict
\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
under the Coulomb-matrix
representation):
the structure encoder

(\Theta_{\varphi},q_{\varphi})\colon{C_{e}}(G)\to Z
,
the structure decoder

(\Theta_{\theta},p_{\theta})\colon Z\to{C_{e}}(G)
,
and the property encoder

(\Theta_{\psi},p_{\psi})\colon\mathbb{R}^{d}\to Z
— the third
network added in
[
89
]
for inverse design,
taking properties to latent, not latent to properties.

p_{\theta}
is a second forward map, not the backward map of a
CGGWZ lens;
the two have different categorical signatures, as the
backward component of a parametric lens must carry a change
object (tangent space, in the smooth case) that
p_{\theta}
’s
signature
Z\to{C_{e}}(G)
does not.
Nor does the encoder–decoder round trip

p_{\theta}\circ q_{\varphi}
produce a 2-morphism of

\mathrm{Para}(\mathcal{C})
:
its deviation from
\mathrm{id}_{{C_{e}}(G)}
measured on a test
set (the QM7-X RMSD of
[
89
]
) is a scalar
training residual.
A 2-morphism of
\mathrm{Para}(\mathcal{C})
is a reparametrisation

r\colon\Theta^{\prime}\to\Theta
satisfying

f_{\theta}\circ(r\otimes\mathrm{id}_{X})=f_{\theta^{\prime}}

(Definition
11.1
), an equation in
\mathcal{C}
,
not a real-valued error.
The forward property-prediction path through the shared
latent approximates

\Pi\circ\sigma_{0}\colon{C_{e}}(G)\to\mathbb{R}^{d}
(the
Born–Oppenheimer ground-state section followed by observable
projection) implicitly, via the joint training objective
rather than a dedicated latent-to-property decoder
(Section
11.6
);
the approximation is numerical, and its error is not a 2-cell
in any 2-category.

The categorical content at the
\mathcal{L}_{5}
–
\mathcal{L}_{6}
interface is
therefore precisely this.
The architecture is three parametric maps of
\mathcal{L}_{5}
-type
through a shared latent.
Its output types — scalar properties in
\mathbb{R}^{d}
along the
forward path through the shared latent, and reconstructed
geometries in
{C_{e}}(G)
from
p_{\theta}
— are not sections
of the Hilbert bundle
{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(N)}\to{C_{e}}(G)
.
No instantiation at any
r\colon I\to\Theta
produces
such a section, and no such instantiation represents the
Berry class
[\gamma_{B}]\in H^{1}({C_{e}}(G)\setminus\mathcal{X}_{01},\mathbb{Z}_{2})
.
The architecture therefore sits at
\mathcal{L}_{5}
-type (non-strict

\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
under the Coulomb-matrix representation;
Section
11.6
) despite its approximation
target
\Pi\circ\sigma_{0}
referring, through
\sigma_{0}
, to
the
\mathcal{L}_{6}
functor
F_{\!6}
.
Section
11.6
works this out for QIM in detail;
Proposition
11.19
of
Section
11.7
promotes the output-type
observation to a structural incompleteness result.

Where the CGGWZ framework sits relative to the
tower

The preceding mathboxes locate each framework by the forgetful
functor above which its vocabulary runs out.
CGGWZ admits no such localisation:
its subject is compositional backpropagation, not the
level-by-level structure the tower resolves.
No
U_{k}\colon\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)\to\mathcal{L}_{k-1}(P)
bounds its reach;
its reach is perpendicular.
Structurally, CGGWZ supplies the 2-categorical backdrop of
Section
11.1
— the 2-category

\mathrm{Para}(\mathcal{C})
, the reparametrisation 2-cells, and the
lax-algebra derivation of the weight-tying comonoid

(!_{\Theta},\Delta_{\Theta})
of condition (C
k
) — but does
not identify a specific (E
k
).
The Berry-class obstruction of
Proposition
11.19
is, in this
light, a statement about the output type of the architecture’s
1-morphisms, not about whether they compose as lenses under
gradient descent.

Bridge to the remainder of the chapter.

The framework-to-level pairings collected above supply the
categorical vocabulary of every subsequent section of this
chapter.
Section
11.3
uses them as the
classification criterion:
the level assigned to a 1-morphism
(\Theta,f_{\theta})
of

\mathrm{Para}(\mathcal{C})
is the highest
k
for which it satisfies
the corresponding (E
k
), and
Table
7
records the resulting
assignments.
Section
11.4
takes the
(E_{5})
lift of NGN as
the structural condition MACE and NequIP satisfy, then asks a
quantitative question the level assignment alone cannot
answer — which morphisms in
\mathcal{L}_{5}(P)(X,Y)
actually lie
in the architecture’s function class

\mathsf{Func}(\Theta,f_{\theta})
— and frames the
corresponding density question on smooth BO potentials as a
conditional under universal-approximation hypotheses.
Section
11.5
recasts the same
(E_{5})

condition in the language of
SE(3)
-equivariant self-attention,
without the NGN’s message-passing substrate.
Section
11.6
works through QIM as the concrete
triple of
\mathcal{L}_{5}
-type maps identified above (non-strict

\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
under the Coulomb-matrix representation),
whose approximation target
\Pi\circ\sigma_{0}
references the

\mathcal{L}_{6}
ground-state section
\sigma_{0}\colon{C_{e}}(G)\to{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(N)}
while the architecture’s scalar output type keeps
it within the
\mathcal{L}_{5}
region.
Section
11.7
names the failure
structurally:
the Berry class

[\gamma_{B}]\in H^{1}({C_{e}}(G)\setminus\mathcal{X}_{01},\mathbb{Z}_{2})
that

F_{\!6}
attaches at conical intersections is expressible in

none
of the level-specific external frameworks collected
here — not in NGN, not in Markov categories, not in string
diagrams — and is equally outside the level-orthogonal
CGGWZ vocabulary, whose subject is gradient composition rather
than output-type structure.
The topological obstruction of that section therefore cannot be
derived by upgrading any of the external vocabularies;
it requires the full
\mathcal{L}_{6}^{\mathrm{Para}}
machinery of
Section
11.1
, a fact the mathboxes closing the
three preceding subsections make unavoidable.

Categorical completeness (Definition
11.5
)
provides the quantitative refinement of every level
assignment:
at level
k
it measures how much of
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)(X,Y)
the
architecture’s function class

\mathsf{Func}(\Theta,f_{\theta})
actually covers.
The bridging material of this section is the prerequisite for
that quantitative question to be well-posed at each level and
for its negative answer at
\mathcal{L}_{6}
to be more than an empirical observation.

§11.3. Classification of machine learning molecular architectures

Table
7
classifies the major ML molecular architectures by the highest tower level
k
for which the function class
\mathsf{Func}(\Theta,f_{\theta})
of a parametric 1-morphism
(\Theta,f_{\theta})
is contained in
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)(X,Y)
— the membership condition
(\mathrm{E}_{k})
of Definition
11.2
.
The function class, defined in
Remark
11.4
, is the set of all morphisms the
architecture can represent as
r
ranges over
\mathcal{C}(I,\Theta)
;
it is independent of any particular training run. The
classification is therefore a statement about what the architecture

can
represent, not about where a specific learned weight
configuration lands.

Three senses of satisfying
(\mathrm{E}_{k})

Level assignment turns on distinguishing three claims any one of
which a reader might intend by saying an architecture “satisfies
level
k
”.

Architectural satisfaction.

\mathsf{Func}(\Theta,f_{\theta})\subseteq\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)(X,Y)
for
every
\theta\in\Theta
. This is
(\mathrm{E}_{k})
, and only
this gives categorical membership of the parametric morphism in

\mathcal{L}_{k}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
.

Training-emergent satisfaction.

A specific
\theta^{*}\in\Theta
obtained by training produces
outputs numerically close to
\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)(X,Y)
on a benchmark.
Other choices of
\theta
need not.

Type compatibility.

The codomain of
f_{\theta}
matches the codomain of

\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
-morphisms (e.g. scalars on
{C_{e}}(G)
), but the

\mathcal{L}_{k}(P)
-defining structure beyond the codomain is not enforced.

The classification below applies the architectural sense strictly.
The recurring failure mode the audit rectifies is upgrading from
training-emergent or type-compatible to architectural without the
corresponding closure in
\mathsf{Func}(\Theta,f_{\theta})
.

The table is ordered by tower level, with the reaction-side region
(stoichiometry, kinetics, mechanism) first, then the configurational
regions
\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
and
\mathcal{L}_{6}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
.
Proposition
11.19

(Section
11.7
) confines every

E(3)
-equivariant scalar-energy architecture to
\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
:
the codomain
\mathbf{Orb}^{\mathrm{Morse}}
cannot accommodate a non-trivial section of

{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(N)}\to{C_{e}}(G)
, and no amount of training, body-order
refinement, or
l_{\max}
-inflation alters the codomain.

Two sub-categories used as classification labels in the table deserve
formal statement before their first appearance.

Classification sub-categories used in the table

Generative
\mathcal{L}_{5}
.
Alongside
\mathcal{L}_{5}(P)
, whose morphisms
are
SE(3)\rtimes\mathrm{Aut}(G)
-equivariant scalar potentials

V\colon{C_{e}}(G)\to\mathbb{R}
with conservative forces
F=-\nabla V
,
define the generative variant
\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{gen}}(P)
whose
morphisms are maps
f\colon\mathrm{Seq}\to{C_{e}}(G)
from an
input space
\mathrm{Seq}
(sequences, labels, latent codes)

into
the configuration orbifold, reversing the direction
of
\mathcal{L}_{5}
-morphisms. The membership condition

(\mathrm{E}_{5}^{\mathrm{gen}})
is that
f
factor through the
quotient
{C_{e}}(G)=\mathbb{R}^{3n}/(SE(3)\rtimes\mathrm{Aut}(G))
well-definedly:
any lift
\widetilde{f}\colon\mathrm{Seq}\to\mathbb{R}^{3n}
must
project to the same class in
{C_{e}}(G)
, regardless of the frame
choice implicit in the lift. Architecturally this is enforced by
making all internal operations that fix or transform a frame
covariant under
SE(3)\rtimes\mathrm{Aut}(G)
, so distinct frame
conventions yield the same orbit. The Para enrichment is

\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para},\mathrm{gen}}(P)
; no PES, no
F_{\!V}
, no dynamics.

Operator-level vs section-level
\mathcal{L}_{6}
.

The
\mathcal{L}_{6}
object is the
U(N)
-gauge Hilbert bundle

{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(N)}\to{C_{e}}(G)
with its Berry connection
A_{mn}^{\mu}
,
seam
\mathcal{X}_{01}
, and class

[\gamma_{B}]\in H^{1}({C_{e}}(G)\setminus\mathcal{X}_{01},\mathbb{Z}_{2})
. Two
architecturally distinct codomains approximate this object. The

operator-level
codomain is

\mathrm{End}({\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{\mathrm{AO}})
, the space of symmetric
operators on a fixed atomic-orbital basis Hilbert space, with

SE(3)
-equivariance of the operator-valued map. The fixed basis
trivialises the bundle globally;
U(N)
gauge freedom on the
fibres is frozen. The
section-level
codomain is a

U(N)
-gauge-equivariant section

\sigma\colon{C_{e}}(G)\setminus\mathcal{X}_{01}\to{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(N)}
,
architecturally required to transform correctly under fibre
reparameterisation and to respect
[\gamma_{B}]
-consistency on
loops encircling
\mathcal{X}_{01}
. The two sub-categories are orthogonal approximations of full

\mathcal{L}_{6}
, not nested: operator-level captures

H_{\mathrm{el}}(\mathbf{R})
completely but freezes the
U(N)

fibre gauge by fixing a basis, while section-level captures a
single gauge-covariant state
\sigma
but not the full operator.
Diagonalising an operator-level output recovers bundle fibres
pointwise but not a canonical global section: the
eigenvector-phase ambiguity around
\mathcal{X}_{01}
makes any lift from
operator-level to section-level non-canonical. Full

\mathcal{L}_{6}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
membership requires both capabilities
simultaneously: operator-valued fidelity and
U(N)
-gauge-covariant
sectioning with
[\gamma_{B}]
-consistency. PhiSNet and
DeepH-E3 reach the operator-level sub-category architecturally;
SPAINN offers a partial (connection-level) approach toward the
section-level sub-category. No architecture in the audit
occupies both sub-categories, and none reaches full

\mathcal{L}_{6}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
.

\{0,1\}^{d}
.
Two distinct tower objects fail to lift through this pipeline.
The free commutative monoid
\mathbb{N}[\mathcal{S}]
is lost first: hashing maps
distinct substructures to the same bit, bit-folding projects to

\{0,1\}
and erases counts, so
\mathsf{Func}(\Theta,\mathrm{fp})

lands in a multiplicity-forgetting quotient of
\mathbb{N}[\mathcal{S}]
strictly
below the free-commutative-monoid structure
\mathcal{L}_{0}(P)
requires.
The Hess functor
F_{\!H}\colon\mathcal{L}_{1}(P)\to B\mathbb{R}
fails consequently:

\mathrm{fp}(r_{1}\circ r_{2})
bears no
\mathbb{R}
-additive relation to

\mathrm{fp}(r_{1})\oplus\mathrm{fp}(r_{2})
, so
(\mathrm{E}_{1})

cannot even be stated in the codomain
\mathrm{fp}
lives in. The
identity
\mathrm{fp}(r)=\mathrm{fp}(r^{\dagger})
produced by the
symmetric difference is not evidence of
\mathcal{L}_{2}
-membership: it

trivialises
the dagger by collapsing forward and reverse
reactions to the identity in the codomain, before
(\cdot)^{\dagger}

has any oriented reaction morphism left to act on. The ceiling is
accordingly the first lossy step in the pipeline:
\mathbb{N}[\mathcal{S}]
is
unrecoverable, and every higher structure depending on it —

F_{\!H}
,
\ker(F_{\!G}^{T})
,
\FP
, the DPO span — is unreachable as a
matter of type, not training.

Kinetic ODE surrogates.

ChemNODE parametrises a vector field

d\Phi/dt=f_{\theta}(\Phi)
on a fixed thermochemical state space

\mathbb{R}^{N_{s}+1}
. No
\mathrm{Sym}(\mathcal{S})
-action is defined on the
index set — species indices are distinguishable MLP channels —
no positivity constraint is imposed on the RHS, and no guarantee is
made that mass or element conservation survives integration.

\mathsf{Func}(\Theta,f_{\theta})
therefore does not land in

\Stoch
(probability is not conserved), nor in the mass-action
subcategory of
\mathcal{L}_{0}(P)
, nor even in the

\mathrm{Sym}(\mathcal{S})
-equivariant part of
\mathcal{L}_{0}(P)
. Follow-up work
adds mass conservation as an auxiliary loss, confirming its
absence from the base architecture. ChemNODE sits strictly below

\mathcal{L}_{0}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
.

CRNN, by contrast, hard-codes a stoichiometric-coefficient layer

\nu\in\mathbb{R}^{N_{s}\times N_{r}}
(continuous, sparsity-regularised
toward integer values but not integrality-constrained
architecturally) as its first operation and composes it with an
exponential activation implementing the mass-action monomial

\prod_{i}X_{i}^{\nu_{ij}}
and Arrhenius kernel

k_{j}(T)=A_{j}T^{b_{j}}\exp(-E_{a,j}/RT)
. The first-layer linear
map is
\mathrm{Sym}(\mathcal{S})
-equivariant by construction, placing
CRNN inside the real-relaxation of
\mathcal{L}_{0}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)

architecturally; convergence to integer
\nu
at a trained
optimum recovers strict
\mathcal{L}_{0}
membership. The composition
yields a deterministic mass-action vector field — a morphism in
the Feinberg–Horn–Jackson category of chemical reaction
networks. But CRNN is not a
\Stoch
-morphism (no CME generator

\Omega
, no stochastic trajectories), not a dagger-category
morphism (forward and reverse
(A,b,E_{a})
are independent, so

\ker(F_{\!G}^{T})
is not preserved and detailed balance is not
enforced), and not a morphism in
\mathcal{L}_{1}(P)
either: the Arrhenius
activation energy
E_{a}
is not
\Delta H
, so it is not the Hess
image of a reaction arrow. CRNN’s correct placement is therefore the

\mathbb{R}
-relaxation of
\mathcal{L}_{0}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)

augmented
by a
deterministic rate law that sits beside, not inside, the

\mathcal{L}_{1}
–
\mathcal{L}_{3}
portion of the tower.

Reaction SMILES sequence models.

Molecular Transformer maps token sequences in
\Sigma^{*}
to token
sequences in
\Sigma^{*}
by autoregressive decoding. No graph
object appears in its type signature: the token stream need not
parse to a molecular graph at all, and when it does, the mapping
from strings to objects of
\mathbf{LGraph}_{P}
is partial and learned.
Atom and charge conservation, bond validity, and

\mathrm{Aut}(G)
-equivariance are all training-emergent rather than
architectural, with documented failures even on in-distribution
benchmarks. The image of
\mathsf{Func}(\Theta,f_{\theta})
does
not lie in the DPO-span category forced by the
\mathcal{L}_{3}\to\mathcal{L}_{4}

pair, so there is no pushout complement on which to claim
\mathcal{L}_{4}

membership; there is not even a
\mathrm{Sym}(\mathcal{S})
-action on the
input side, since distinct SMILES orderings of the same reactant
multiset are distinct input sequences. The architectural ceiling
is
\mathbb{N}[\mathcal{S}]
itself: conservation of species multiplicities is not
enforced by construction, and Molecular Transformer sits strictly
below
\mathcal{L}_{0}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
.

The
\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}
(invariant) block.

All nine architectures in this block target a scalar potential

V\colon{C_{e}}(G)\to\mathbb{R}
with forces recovered by
autodifferentiation on the conservative head. Coulomb matrix and
SOAP, as standalone feature maps, sit below
\mathcal{L}_{5}
; paired with
a regressor (KRR, GAP) they realise
\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
(invariant).
Behler–Parrinello and ANI enforce

O(3)\times\mathrm{Sym}(\mathcal{S})\times\mathbb{R}^{3}
-invariance by
construction via atom-centred symmetry functions; SchNet achieves
the same invariances via continuous-filter convolutions with
pairwise-distance-dependent filters. DimeNet enriches the message
with 3-body angles; GemNet extends to 4-body dihedrals with a
universal-approximation guarantee for
SE(3)
-invariant
continuous functions on
{C_{e}}(G)
at the conservative head. In all
these cases the outputs are scalar: internal rotationally
covariant features are discharged through an invariant readout.
ALIGNN takes the line-graph perspective to expose bond–bond
angles, again at invariant output. PaiNN is the sole borderline
case: its
l{=}0
and
l{=}1
internal features are

O(3)
-equivariant by construction, and its non-energy heads
(dipoles, polarizabilities) exit
\mathbf{Orb}^{\mathrm{Morse}}
— but they land in
rank-
\leq 2
tensor bundles over
{C_{e}}(G)
that are topologically
trivial (no eigenvalue-crossing locus seeds a non-trivial Chern
class), so nothing here advances to the topologically non-trivial

{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{el}}}^{(N)}\to{C_{e}}(G)
that
\mathcal{L}_{6}
demands. For all nine, the
ceiling is the same: no
SE(3)
-equivariant scalar force field
provides a section of
U_{6}\colon\mathbf{HilbBund}\to\mathbf{Orb}^{\mathrm{Morse}}
, and
the class
[\gamma_{B}]\in H^{1}({C_{e}}(G)\setminus\mathcal{X}_{01},\mathbb{Z}_{2})
is
not a functional of any real-valued
V

(Proposition
11.19
). The GemNet
direct-force variant falls out of
\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}(P)
altogether:
when
F
is predicted as a separate head rather than as
-\nabla V
,
the morphism exits the conservative-force-field category and fails

(\mathrm{E}_{5})
strictly.

The
\mathcal{L}_{5}^{\mathrm{Para}}
(equivariant) block.

NequIP, MACE, MACE-MP-0, Allegro, So3krates, SO3LR, Equiformer,
and eSEN all satisfy
(\mathrm{E}_{5})
as an architectural
guarantee. Their internal features carry
O(3)
irrep labels with

l\leq l_{\max}
, composed via e3nn Clebsch–Gordan products,
eSCN
SO(2)
convolutions, or
SE(3)
-equivariant self-attention,
and the energy head reduces to a scalar. The distinctions among
them are not tower-level distinctions. MACE adds body-order via
the atomic cluster expansion; a separate observation, developed
in Section
11.4

(Proposition
11.9
), is that the
MACE-specific forgetful
U_{4}
cannot cleanly separate
\mathcal{L}_{4}

bond topology from
\mathcal{L}_{5}
geometry in the internal representation.
MACE-MP-0 is MACE trained at foundation-model scale; its codomain
is unchanged. Allegro replaces atom-centred message passing with
iterated pairwise tensor products, giving a receptive field
bounded by
r_{\mathrm{cut}}
regardless of depth. So3krates uses

SE(3)
-equivariant self-attention in spherical-harmonic
coordinates with in-principle-unbounded range. SO3LR augments the
So3krates core with explicit analytical baselines so that
